en: The Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī-ratna-prabhāsa Sūtra, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master and State Preceptor Dharma-dhātu, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa and Subject Fa-tian, at Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India.
Translated by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard:

At one time the Bhagavān was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus numbering in the hundreds of thousands. He had perfected all pure dharmas (*śukladharma*), let out the great lion’s roar, possessed immeasurable wisdom, and had attained great and excellent benefit. He was also accompanied by a multitude of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, whose names were:
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, Ratnamudrāhasta Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, and Nityadarśana Bodhisattva... [and so forth].
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sāgaramati, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Guṇavyūha,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Puṇyasvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāmati, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Guṇavibhūṣaṇa,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramati, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajra...
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Prabhāsa, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrāyudha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Suvajra,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Dharaṇīdhara, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvadharmaprakāśana,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dṛḍhamati, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraśrī,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Apāyajaha, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvakleśapraśamanamati.
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Peaceful Gait, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Free from Grasping and Abandoning,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sandalwood Fragrance, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ocean Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Difficult to Conquer,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jewel Victor, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Wisdom Practice;
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Prajñākūṭa, Gandhavyūha, and Maitreya— these and countless other Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas—
all dwell in the gate of the samādhi of courageous and fierce inconceivable liberation, and have also attained immeasurable sounds that are never in vain.
One contemplates all sounds and all Buddha-fields as tranquil and serene; their lifespans are immeasurable, they have attained great renown,
they are unattached to the three realms, and they are indestructible, with those who possess all-knowledge as their retinue.

They give birth to immeasurable samādhis and samāpattis, are able to fulfill the aspirations of all beings, and because they have all reached the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they attain non-empty actions of body, speech, and mind; they abide in the immeasurable practices and vows of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), and they thoroughly comprehend the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
All such great bodhisattvas as these had come to the assembly and were seated.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra rose from his seat within the assembly, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"How should one know the dharma-realm?
The Buddha said, "Good son!..."
This dharma-realm is devoid of intrinsic nature, and there is no one who can know it. Why is this?
O son of good family!

Like space, it is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), yet not apart from conceptual proliferation; it is neither grasping nor abandoning, neither having an intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) nor lacking an intrinsic nature, and it has no location.
"Good son! Therefore, the dharma-realm should be known in this way.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How should the dharma-realm abide?
The Buddha said:
“Good son! Since even a location does not exist, how much less could there be any dwelling? Good son!”
This dharmadhātu is inconceivable, ineffable, devoid of intrinsic nature, and incapable of being fully known.
Good son! That nature of the dharmadhātu cannot be known and cannot be seen.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How many kinds of bodhi are there?”
The Buddha said,
"Good son! Bodhi has immeasurable characteristics that cannot be measured."
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said:
“World-Honored One, how,
furthermore, is the dharma-realm to be distinguished?”
The Buddha said,
“Good son! The Dharma-realm is fundamentally without discrimination.”
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said:
“World-Honored One!
If the dharma-realm is indivisible, how can ordinary sentient beings understand it?”
The Buddha said,
"Good son! Those who possess discrimination are all deluded and ignorant sentient beings, who give rise to discrimination within that which is non-discriminative."
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata’s bodhi is thus profoundly deep, subtle, and difficult to understand.”
The Buddha said: “Good son! So it is, so it is!”
"It is as you have said.
The Buddha further addressed him, saying: "Good son!"
“Bodhi is all phenomena; being free from all conceptual proliferation, it is therefore without discrimination.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī was also seated in the assembly. He rose from his seat, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"We pray that you will explain for us this Dharma-gate of the Jewel Radiance Dhāraṇī.
The Buddha said, "Good sons!..."
"You should now question that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvadharmanidhānagarbhapratibhāna; he will explain it for you.
Thereupon, the youth Mañjuśrī, before the Tathāgata, joined his ten fingers and palms together, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"The Tathāgata is the All-Knowing One and the All-Seeing One; why then does he not speak?
The Buddha said, "Good son!..."
"Because there are such great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as these, for this reason the Tathāgata does not speak. Mañjuśrī said:
"So it is, World-Honored One!"
"Why does the Tathāgata not speak for himself? He abandons us!
The Buddha said:
“Good son! It is not because I abandon the realm of sentient beings. Good son!”
"This is because he wishes to demonstrate that the comparisons and calculations spoken by those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are inconceivable.
Then, the youth Mañjuśrī again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"I only pray that the Tathāgata, with immeasurable great compassion, will expound for me this Dharma-gate of the Jewel Radiance Dhāraṇī.
The Buddha said, "Good son!"
If you now question this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, he will surely explain this Dharma-gate for you.
Son of good family!
You should know that the wisdom of this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is immeasurable.
Mañjuśrī said, “If the Tathāgata commands me to question that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, I shall now do so.
The Buddha said:
“Mañjuśrī! You yourself have attained samādhi-gates as numerous as atoms; for what reason, then, do you question the Tathāgata? Mañjuśrī replied:
“World-Honored One!
Not only the Dharma spoken by a single Buddha, but even the true nature of reality (tathatā) as taught by all Tathāgatas, I am able to remember and maintain without forgetting, just as I do today.”
The Buddha said: “Excellent, excellent!
Son of good family!”
“You have now spoken well,” the Buddha said. “Mañjuśrī!”
"You should now question this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra regarding the dharma-gate of dhāraṇī.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra has profoundly realized the Mahāyāna practice of the Dharma of the true mark.
The Buddha said, "Good son!
"You are all sons of the Sovereign Dharma King; how could you be otherwise? Good sons!
Your merit and virtue are immeasurable; you have thoroughly realized the dharma of emptiness and attained the inconceivable gates of liberation and samādhi."

At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī, receiving the holy command of the Buddha, joined his ten fingers and palms together before the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra; with single-minded reverence, he addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, saying:
“O Son of the Buddha!
"I pray that you will explain for me the Dharma-gate of two syllables.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said: "Good son!
"What are these two characters about which you now inquire?
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!"
"What are the characteristics of these two terms, 'awakening' and 'the one who awakens'?
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva replied,
"O Son of the Buddha!..."

Awakening is fundamentally without marks, without intrinsic nature, inconceivable, peerless, free from all conceptual proliferation, yet not apart from conceptual proliferation; it is beyond the reach of speech and deliberation.
"Good son! For this reason, the awakened nature of all Buddhas is thus. Mañjuśrī said:
“O Son of the Buddha!
If the Buddha-dharma is not conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), why does the Buddha-dharma speak in such a manner?
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
“O Son of the Buddha!
Because it transcends verbal expression, it is described in this way. Mañjuśrī said:
“O Son of the Buddha!
How does one transcend verbal expression?
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva replied:
“Mañjuśrī! Wisdom is beyond verbal expression. Mañjuśrī replied:
“O Son of the Buddha!
How is wisdom known?
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva replied:
“Mañjuśrī, it is that wisdom is without intrinsic nature, yet wisdom is not without intrinsic nature. Mañjuśrī said:
“O Son of the Buddha!
How is it that wisdom has no intrinsic nature, yet wisdom is not without intrinsic nature?
How should one explain the Dharma of the Three Vehicles?”
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said:
"Mañjuśrī! The dharma-realm is free from defilement; how can there be any speaking of it?"
Mañjuśrī said: "In what way are all phenomena likewise without intrinsic nature?
And in what sense is the nature of the Tathāgata described as untainted?"
“Because the nature of the five aggregates cannot be apprehended.
Mañjuśrī said: “How could there be conceptual proliferation regarding bodhi?”
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said:
"O Son of the Buddha!
Awakening is without conceptual proliferation, yet it is not apart from conceptual proliferation."
"This Bodhi, whether characterized by conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) or free from conceptual proliferation, is neither speech nor discourse.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Good son! As you have said, this inconceivable Dharma-gate is profound and far-reaching; these are words of truth that none among gods or humans can comprehend."
Then the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
All dharmas are unknowable, invisible, and there is no dharma that can be spoken.”
The Buddha said: "Good son, it is so! It is so!"
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This pure Dharma-gate is difficult to understand and difficult to know.”
The Buddha said: "Good son, it is so! It is so!"
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Samantabhadra Bodhisattva has skillfully expounded such a Dharma-gate of purity.”
The Buddha said: "Good son, it is so! It is so!"
"Furthermore, son of good family!
All dharmas are pure in this way; they pour down the great rain of Dharma.
At that time, the Brahmin Mahāśāla, Equal and Quiescent, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This inconceivable, equal enlightenment is free from the marks of letters, invisible, and devoid of all marks of form.
The Buddha said:
“Good son! So it is! So it is!”
"The nature of the dharma-realm is free from [all things], and all marks are extinguished.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"What are the characteristics of emptiness?
Is it sound, is it form, or is it these marks and signs?
The Buddha said:
“Mañjuśrī! Emptiness is free from sound and form, and is free from all verbal expression, yet it is not apart from verbal expression.
Son of good family!
The nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is thus: it is called "emptiness" because emptiness is free from words, and it is called "emptiness" because it is beyond verbal expression.
Good son! Emptiness is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of all phenomena.
At that time, the Elder Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
does the Tathāgata regard this Bodhisattva of Great Manifestations and Inconceivable Liberation?”
The Buddha addressed the Elder Śāriputra, saying:
"The wisdom of this Arhat is vastly inferior to the wisdom of a Bodhisattva who has first resolved to attain enlightenment; how much more so, then, for this Bodhisattva!"
"Why is this? A bodhisattva who has first resolved to attain awakening shall achieve buddhahood, whereas an arhat ultimately cannot.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of All Dharmas addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
As the Buddha has taught, I fully understand it all.
Should this śrāvaka not obtain the dharma of a śrāvaka?”
The Buddha said,
"Good son! It is not that these śrāvakas do not attain the dharma of the śrāvakas."
"Furthermore, son of good family!
If a śrāvaka were to debate with a bodhisattva, their wisdom would differ; therefore, the former cannot reach the level of the latter.
At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the Tathāgata says this Śāriputra has attained the foremost wisdom?
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
"As I have said, in reality nothing is attained.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī spoke to the Elder Śāriputra, saying: "Elder!..."
"How have you attained the Dharma of the śrāvakas? Śāriputra replied,
"This is beyond my capacity."
Mañjuśrī said: "Are you not, by any chance, an ordinary person?
[The other] replied: "No!"
"Good son," Mañjuśrī said, "Śāriputra!..."
"How should you train? Śāriputra replied,
"I have nothing to learn."
Mañjuśrī said, "How does one attain the foremost wisdom? Śāriputra replied:
“I am also not capable.
Mañjuśrī spoke again to the Elder Śāriputra, saying:
“Since you are neither an ordinary person nor the foremost in wisdom, who are you?”
Śāriputra said: "Good son! I, too, do not know."
"Your wisdom is immeasurable, like a vast ocean; therefore, I do not consider myself a suitable opponent for debate with you.
Mañjuśrī said, "Venerable Śāriputra!"
"Do not speak thus; you yourself are of venerable age and long-standing virtue, so why do you practice such humility?
Śāriputra said, "O son of good family!
"Although I am advanced in years, I possess neither virtue nor realization. Furthermore, good son!
It is like all the myriad differentiated phenomena, which, like a great mountain, are shattered into dust by a single strike of a vajra."
"Good son! You are also like this:

the measure of wisdom within a single pore, which is equal to the number of atoms, is such that all sentient beings—even if they were all exactly like me—would still not be able to reach it, good son!"
How much less so for me alone?
Therefore, I am likewise unable to undertake this task. Good son!
Just as a great and wicked elephant, though its body is massive and its strength is immense, can be subdued by a person using a hook, so too am I,
O son of good family!
Why is this? You possess great power of wisdom, whereas my strength is feeble.
O son of good family!
“You are equal to great nāgas; how could my strength oppose that of such venerable ones?
The Elder Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
It is like a person born blind who wishes to travel to another state; while on the road, they will certainly be unable to see that city, so how could they possibly travel throughout it?
"Good son! This is also like that:
I am like that blind man before you; I am likewise now. The Buddha-way is vast and remote, having come from a great distance; how can it be known?"
The Buddha told Śāriputra: "Do not speak thus!
The majestic power of the Tathāgata is such that it can cause all sentient beings to obtain this Dharma even if they merely hear it for a brief moment."
"Śāriputra! How much more so for you, who have already attained this inconceivable samādhi.
At that time, when the World-Honored One preached this Dharma, ninety-two thousand beings among gods and humans all attained this Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dharmamati, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, immediately entered a samādhi called the "Jewel Radiance of Boundless Correspondence of Bodhisattvas."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Dharmamati immediately entered worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten thousand Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions; in every single direction, there appeared before him ten thousand Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the atoms within those Buddha-fields.
Then those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, spoke to the Bodhisattva Dharmamati, saying:
"As it is in one direction, so it is in all ten directions.
Those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent, Dharmamati!
It is because you are able to enter this bodhisattva samādhi of boundless correspondence.”
Furthermore, son of good family!

At that time, in each and every direction, there were as many stations of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in ten thousand Buddha-fields of these ten directions. All those Tathāgatas bore the same name; they were all the World-Honored One Vairocana Tathāgata. By virtue of the power of his original vows and his primordial majesty, they attained great and excellent benefits, even to the point of turning the Great Wheel of Dharma.
All those Buddhas spoke these verses in unison:
"The Buddha-wisdom is fundamentally pure, Pervading everywhere throughout the Dharma-realm;
Likewise, when observing the realm of sentient beings, It enters everywhere with unimpeded wisdom."
Through the gateway of peerless correspondence, skilled in all languages,
one swiftly attains omniscience; having perfected all phenomena and brought the wisdom of the three times to full completion, one skillfully expounds such a Dharma.
“Good son! By the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, you now proclaim this Dharma-gate of the ten stages of the bodhisattva.

At that time, each of those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, used their unimpeded wisdom to shine upon the Bodhisattva Dharmamati, whereby he further attained such samādhi-gates as: the unimpeded, the uninterrupted, the non-empty dharma, the non-empty wisdom, the untainted, the boundless, the inexhaustible, the neither-coming-nor-going, the limitless, and the intrinsic nature of non-attachment. He attained such samādhi-gates as these.
At that time, those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, each extended their right hand and stroked the crown of the head of the Bodhisattva Dharmamati.
Once those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, had finished stroking the Bodhisattva’s crown, the Bodhisattva Dharmamati immediately arose from samādhi and addressed the Bodhisattvas, saying:
"Sons of the Buddha!
The lineage of Bodhisattvas is vast and immeasurable, pervading the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of empty space.
O Son of the Buddha!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already been born within the lineage of past Tathāgatas, are now being born within the lineage of present Tathāgatas, and shall be born within the lineage of future Tathāgatas.
At that time, those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas addressed the Bodhisattva Dharmamati, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!
As you have said, how do those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas come to be born into the lineage of the Tathāgatas of the past, present, and future?"
Furthermore, how is it said that those bodhisattvas have attained the bodhisattva abodes?
Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas addressed the bodhisattva Dharmamati, saying:
“O Son of the Buddha!

Excellent! We pray that you will expound for us this Dharma-gate of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; it was spoken by the Buddhas of the past, is being spoken by the Buddhas of the present, and will be spoken by the Buddhas of the future.
“O Son of the Buddha!
How does one explain the ten stages of the bodhisattva’s practice of the Dharma?
They are as follows:”

1. The Dwelling of Generating the Mind; 2. The Dwelling of Preparing the Ground; 3. The Dwelling of Correspondence; 4. The Dwelling of Noble Birth; 5. The Dwelling of Fulfillment of Skillful Means; 6. The Dwelling of the Right Mind; 7. The Dwelling of Non-retrogression; 8. The Dwelling of Youthful Truth; 9. The Dwelling of the Prince; 10. The Dwelling of Empowerment.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten stages of the Dharma-practice of Bodhisattvas.
They have been taught by all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present; they are being taught now; and they shall be taught in the future.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is that Bodhisattva’s dwelling of the production of the thought of enlightenment?

It means that this Bodhisattva beholds the physical marks of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, which are majestic, extraordinary, exquisite, and peerless in their vastness; and [beholds] their vast preaching of the Dharma and their vast transformation of sentient beings.”
Having witnessed such vast manifestations and heard the extensive Dharma, they attained what they had never experienced before.

Furthermore, seeing sentient beings in such suffering and distress, the Bodhisattvas resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in order to seek the *sarvajñatā* and *sarvākārajñatā* of the Tathāgata; therefore, this is called the Stage of Initial Resolve (*prathamacittotpādavihāra*).
Furthermore, one studies these ten powers. What are the ten? They are: first, the power of knowing what is possible and what is impossible;

second, the power of knowing the ripening of karmic results of merit in the past, present, and future; third, the power of knowing the meditative concentrations, liberations, and samādhis; fourth, the power of knowing the paths leading to all destinations; fifth, the power of knowing the infinite variety of elements; sixth, the power of knowing the infinite variety of inclinations; seventh, the power of knowing the superior and inferior faculties; eighth, the power of recollecting former abodes; ninth, the power of the divine eye; and tenth, the power of the outflows-free knowledge.

O Son of the Buddha! Because this bodhisattva who has first resolved upon enlightenment should study these powers of the ten stages; because that bodhisattva who has first resolved upon enlightenment, at all times, reverently makes offerings to all Tathāgatas; because that bodhisattva dwells in praise; because he is the most supreme and foremost lord of the world; because he seeks the immeasurable, most supreme wisdom of a Buddha; because he seeks the samādhi corresponding to tranquility; because he distances himself from saṃsāra; because he turns the wheel of the true Dharma; and because he rescues and delivers all sentient beings afflicted by suffering.

Why is this? Because they have resolved their minds toward the true Dharma, listening to it, receiving it, and drawing near to it; because they remain free from all distraction and maintain an uninterrupted continuity.
O Son of the Buddha!
Therefore, this is called the Bodhisattva’s Dwelling of the Initial Resolve.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, what is called the Bodhisattva’s Dwelling of Cultivating the Ground?"
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva dwelling in the Stage of Preparing the Ground first gives rise to ten kinds of mind for the sake of all sentient beings. What are these ten?

That is to say: the mind of faith, the mind of mindfulness, the mind of diligence, the mind of wisdom, the mind of aspiration, the mind of ethical discipline, the mind of protecting the Dharma, the mind of relinquishment, the mind of meditative concentration, and the mind of dedication.
O Son of the Buddha!
Because this Bodhisattva dwelling in the Stage of Preparing the Ground further gives rise to these ten kinds of mind,
O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva dwelling in the Stage of Preparing the Ground constantly maintains mindfulness of extensive learning without interruption; because he always delights in serving spiritual friends, attending upon and drawing near to them; because he is able to maintain vigilant awareness at all times; because his speech is humble and respectful; because he seeks firm and fearless wisdom; because he sets out toward the wisdom of enlightenment; because he aspires with vigor to the wisdom of tranquility; and because he aspires to the sublime Dharma free from all falsehoods, his mind is not deluded.

Why is this? It is because they have given rise to such a sincere mind to seek all Buddha-dharmas; thus, wherever there is a place of the holy Dharma in any direction, they personally go there to listen to, receive, and attend upon it, remaining free from all distraction, continuing without interruption, and never abandoning it for even a moment.
O Son of the Buddha!
For this reason, it is called the Bodhisattva’s Dwelling of Cultivating the Ground.
O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, what is meant by the "dwelling in accordance" of a bodhisattva?
O Son of the Buddha!
This bodhisattva dwelling in accordance has ten objects of observation through which they seek all dharmas.

What are these ten? They are: seeking all unsurpassed dharmas; distancing oneself from all sorrow and suffering; contemplating that dharmas lack intrinsic nature; [seeing that] they are empty and devoid of substantial characteristics; that all dharmas are not permanent; that all dharmas are immeasurable; being free from all doubt and confusion; being unchangeable; being neither existent nor non-existent; and being neither grasped nor abandoned.
O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva dwelling in Correspondence further contemplates the equality of all realms of sentient beings, the equality of the Dharma-realm, the equality of the world-realms, and the equality of the earth element; likewise, the water element, fire element, wind element, space element, the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm—all such realms are entirely equal.
Why is this? It is because all such phenomena are equal in their intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*).

Seeking the supreme Dharma, they travel to the ten directions to approach and listen to the teachings before all Buddhas; remaining free from distraction, they maintain a continuous succession of moments of thought without interruption.
O Son of the Buddha!
For this reason, it is called the Bodhisattva’s Abode of Correspondence.
O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, what is called the Bodhisattva’s Dwelling of Noble Birth?
It is so named because one attains birth through ten kinds of perfect, pure karma and understands the explanations of the noble teachings. What are these ten?

It means that whatever Dharma this Bodhisattva preaches, the assembly will surely revere and accept it; it will gradually increase, becoming firm and non-retrogressive. They will thoroughly comprehend all phenomena (*dharmas*), observing that all worlds are without destruction or extinction; observing that the nature of all karma is free from delusive conceptualization (*vikalpa*); observing that all karmic retributions are without grasping or rejecting; observing that saṃsāra has no characteristics of coming or going; and observing that nirvāṇa is profoundly still and tranquil.
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva dwelling in the state of noble birth attains these ten kinds of perfected pure karma because he understands the explanations of the sacred words.
Furthermore, it is said: O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva dwelling in the Stage of Noble Birth contemplates the equality of the Buddhas of the past because he constantly maintains mindfulness in an uninterrupted succession; he contemplates the equality of the Buddhas of the future because he vows to train accordingly; and he contemplates the equality of the Buddhas of the present because he diligently practices their teachings.

Contemplating that all Buddha-dharmas are thus equal, one thereby attains the limits of the past, the future, and the present; meeting with them throughout these three periods, one practices in this manner, maintaining mindfulness without forgetfulness, and reverently honors all Buddha-dharmas with earnest devotion.

Furthermore, one contemplates the study of the Buddha-dharma of the past, because it increases through equality; one likewise studies the Buddha-dharma of the future, because it increases through equality; and one contemplates the Buddha-dharma of the present, because it increases through equality.
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva dwelling in the state of Noble Birth observes in this way, inclining toward all Buddha-dharmas, which are universally equal, for the sake of increasing and cultivating them.

Why is this? It is because they abide in the most supreme reality where the three periods of time are equal, being free from all artifice; thus, even upon hearing that such a Dharma exists in another direction, they personally travel there, seeking it with diligent vigor, their minds undistracted, their mindfulness continuous and uninterrupted from moment to moment.
O Son of the Buddha!
For this reason, this is called the Bodhisattva’s Dwelling of Noble Birth.
O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, what is called the Bodhisattva’s dwelling in the perfection of skillful means?
O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva dwelling in the perfection of skillful means contemplates the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* realms of sentient beings—realms that are inconceivable, peerless, and equal to space; which are neither born nor extinguished, whose intrinsic nature is pure, and which are identical to the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) and equal to the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*). To observe all sentient beings in this manner is called the Bodhisattva’s dwelling in the perfection of skillful means.
O Son of the Buddha!

For a bodhisattva who dwells in the perfection of these skillful means, there are ten matters for which all the virtuous deeds they cultivate are intended for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings through skillful means: namely, to cause all sentient beings not to regress from the mind set on the unsurpassed path; to cherish all sentient beings and never abandon them; to provide benefit and peace to all sentient beings; out of compassion for all sentient beings; desiring to cause all sentient beings to attain the inconceivable path of liberation; to wash away the defilements of karma of all sentient beings; to gather and subdue all sentient beings; desiring to cause all sentient beings to rejoice without weariness; to guide all sentient beings by means of various skillful means; and desiring to cause all sentient beings to ultimately attain the bliss of nirvāṇa and cessation.
O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva dwelling in the perfection of skillful means, having heard such a Dharma being taught in that other direction, personally travels there to diligently seek and practice it, with a mind free from distraction, maintaining a continuous succession of thoughts without interruption.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva’s dwelling in the perfection of skillful means.
O Son of the Buddha!"
Furthermore, what is called the Bodhisattva’s Dwelling in the Correct Mind?
O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva in the Dwelling of the Correct Mind possesses ten kinds of dharmas that they should joyfully hear, diligently seek with resolute intent, and thereby attain the Dwelling in the Correct Mind within the Buddha-dharma.
O Son of the Buddha!
What are the ten? They are:
by teaching that the Buddha has form and is formless, one attains the abiding of right mind within the Buddha-dharma;
He teaches that there are forms and formlessnesses, and thereby attains abiding in the right mind within the Buddha-dharma;
he teaches that the practices performed by Bodhisattvas have form and are formless, and thereby attains abiding in the right mind within the Buddha-dharma.

In this way, he proceeds to teach about this realm of sentient beings, the great realm of sentient beings, the realm of sentient beings with afflictions, the realm of sentient beings without afflictions, the realm of easily transformed sentient beings, and the realm of difficult-to-transform sentient beings; and so on, up to the great Dharma-realm, the originating Dharma-realm, the world with form, the world without form, the world with phenomena, and the world without phenomena.
O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva abiding in the stage of Right Mindfulness (samyak-citta-vihāra) hears this Dharma within the teachings of the Buddha; thus, it is called the Bodhisattva attaining the stage of Right Mindfulness.
O Son of the Buddha!

Because this bodhisattva abiding in the stage of Right Mindfulness further hears these ten kinds of dharmas, they enter into the principle and seek it with diligence, even hearing all unsurpassed dharmas and practicing and studying them all.
What are these ten? They are:

signlessness, absence of intrinsic nature, lack of reality, non-defilement, remoteness, non-attachment, absence of self-nature, being like an illusion, being like a dream, and freedom from all doubt and confusion.
Having heard all these dharmas in this manner, one should diligently practice them.
Why is this? Because it is for the sake of the bodhisattva who abides with a correct mind, so that they may enter the gateway to the true dharma.

In this manner, even upon hearing such teachings being expounded in other directions, they personally travel there to seek and practice them with diligence; their minds remain undistracted, with mindfulness succeeding moment by moment without interruption.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva’s Abiding in the Rectified Mind.
O Son of the Buddha!"
Furthermore, what is called the Bodhisattva’s Stage of Non-retrogression?
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva in the stage of non-retrogression hears the ten dharmas of non-attachment and, because of this, does not turn back from the mind set upon the Buddha-dharma.
What are these ten? They are:
hearing that there is neither a Buddha nor no Buddha, because this bodhisattva does not regress in their mind regarding the Buddha-dharma;
hearing that there is neither a dharma nor no dharma, because they do not regress in their mind regarding the Buddha-dharma.
There is no bodhisattva, yet there is not no bodhisattva, because they do not regress from the mind of the Buddha-dharma;

there is no grasping of a bodhisattva, yet there is not no grasping of a bodhisattva; there is no departing from bodhisattva practice, yet there is not no departing from bodhisattva practice; a bodhisattva is neither born nor unborn, because they do not regress from the mind of the Buddha-dharma.

The Buddhas of the past have not gone, yet they have not not gone; the Buddhas of the future have not come, yet they have not not come; the Buddhas of the present do not abide, yet they do not not abide. Thus, the Buddhas of the three periods of time are equal in wisdom, of one mark which is markless, neither exhausted nor inexhaustible, and free from all obstructions.
Because this bodhisattva has heard such a Dharma and does not regress in his mind regarding the Buddha-dharma,
O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva’s Stage of Non-regression.
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva dwelling in the stage of Non-retrogression further hears ten kinds of teachings and is able to practice them. What are these ten? They are:

hearing that because one diligently practices all phenomena for the sake of both the one and the many sentient beings, this ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya) constitutes the dependent origination of both the one and the many; because it is the ultimate truth, it is both with nature and without nature, both with characteristics and without characteristics, both with form and without form, and is free from all marks and signs. Thus, his mind attains certainty, and he practices with earnest diligence.

Why is this? It is because, having heard all such phenomena (*dharmas*) in their entirety—comprehending their causes and effects thoroughly and attaining unimpeded penetration into the true nature of reality—one brings them to maturity and full understanding;

and so it continues until, hearing such teachings being expounded in other regions, one personally travels there to seek and practice them with diligence, maintaining an undistracted mind in a continuous succession of moments without interruption.
O Son of the Buddha!
For this reason, it is called the Bodhisattva’s Stage of Non-retrogression.
O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, what is called the Bodhisattva’s Abode of Youthful Truth?
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva in the Abode of Youthful Truth attains ten kinds of dharmas.

What are the ten? They are: attaining purity of bodily action, purity of verbal action, and purity of mental action; being able to observe the arising of thoughts and movements of mind in all sentient beings; being able to fully comprehend whatever actions those sentient beings perform; being able to know such liberation of sentient beings; and being able to know the various realms of sentient beings, the various dharma-realms, the various worlds, as well as the earth element, water element, fire element, wind element, space element, desire realm, form realm, and formless realm—being able to fully comprehend all such realms, and manifesting supernormal powers with such vigor that they arrive wherever they intend.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva’s Abode of Youthful Truth.
O Son of the Buddha!
This bodhisattva dwelling in the stage of "True Youth" further hears ten kinds of dharmas and is able to practice them. What are these ten? They are: hearing the wisdom of a single buddha-field;

shaking all buddha-fields; contemplating all buddha-fields; seeking out all buddha-fields; traveling through all buddha-fields; proceeding to incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) worlds; inquiring into the meaning and intent of incalculable teachings; remaining far removed from the various distinctions of intrinsic nature; and, by giving rise to a single thought-moment, being able to pervade incalculable buddha-fields through listening, hearing, and practicing.
Why is this? It is because they have heard such true Dharma and have brought about the full maturation and understanding of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*).

In this manner, even when hearing such Dharma being taught in other regions, they personally travel there to seek it with diligence and practice it, their minds remaining undistracted, their mindfulness continuing in succession without interruption.
O Son of the Buddha!
For this reason, this is called the Bodhisattva’s Dwelling of Youthful Truth.
O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, what is called the Bodhisattva’s Dwelling of the Dharma Prince?
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva in the Dwelling of the Dharma Prince possesses ten kinds of dharmas, all of which he is able to fully comprehend.

What are these ten? They are: being able to know the places where all sentient beings are born; being able to know the afflictions of all sentient beings; being able to know the attachments of all sentient beings; being able to know the locations of all sentient beings; being able to know the profound and wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas; being able to know the expedient means and true nature of all Buddhas; being able to know the various differentiated phenomena of the worlds; being able to know the wisdom of all Buddhas of the three periods of time—past, future, and present; being able to know that all worldly phenomena are vast yet lack solidity; and being able to know the true nature which is suchness, serene, and quiescent.
O Son of the Buddha!
For this reason, it is called the Bodhisattva Stage of the Dharma Prince.
O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, this Bodhisattva dwelling as a Dharma Prince has ten further dharmas that he should diligently cultivate.

What are these ten? They are: being well-trained in all the various activities of royal cities; being skilled in all the rites and music of royal cities; being skilled in the stable governance of all royal cities; being skilled in entering all royal cities; being skilled in freely and universally traveling through all royal cities; abiding in the consecration of a Dharma King; abiding in the observation of a Dharma King; attaining the sovereign power of a Dharma King; succeeding to the rank of a Dharma King; and abiding in the eloquent discourse of a Dharma King.
Why is this? It is because they cultivate all unimpeded and true dharmas.

In this way, even when hearing such dharmas being taught in other directions, they personally travel there to diligently seek and practice them, with minds undistracted, in continuous succession from moment to moment, without interruption.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva’s Dwelling of the Dharma Prince.
O Son of the Buddha!"
Furthermore, what is called the Bodhisattva’s stage of consecration (*abhiṣeka-vihāra*)?
This bodhisattva attains ten kinds of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*). What are these ten?
That is to say: because it can cause countless worlds to shake in various ways;
because it can illuminate countless worlds in various ways;
and because it can observe countless worlds in various ways.
Because they are able to simultaneously and single-mindedly cultivate practice across various incalculable worlds;
because they are able to accomplish various virtuous deeds across incalculable worlds;
and because they are able to simultaneously know the diverse mentalities of various sentient beings across incalculable worlds.
Because they are able to simultaneously engage with the various mental activities of every single sentient being in incalculable worlds;
because they are able to simultaneously cause every single sentient being in incalculable worlds, who possess various faculties and capacities, to understand and realize [the truth];
and because they are able to teach and transform the various sentient beings in incalculable worlds.
Because he is able to fully know the mental activities of all incalculable sentient beings.
Furthermore, son of good family,
this Bodhisattva dwelling in the stage of Empowerment performs Buddha-deeds through secret and hidden applications that no one can perceive.

Why is this so? It is because one cannot know their physical actions, nor can one know their verbal actions, nor can one know their mental actions; one cannot know their manifestations, nor can one know their observation of various transformations; one cannot know the deeds they performed in the past, nor can one know all the deeds they perform in a single kṣaṇa; one cannot know their observation of wisdom, nor can one know their minds and intentions, nor can one know the functioning of their omniscience.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is because even Bodhisattvas from those dwelling on the stage of Empowerment up to those in the rank of Prince of the Dharma can never know it.
O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva at the stage of consecration further hears of the ten abodes of the Buddha, the World-Honored One.

What are these ten? They are: hearing of the wisdom of the three periods of time; the wisdom of the Buddha; the wisdom of the Dharma; the wisdom that discriminates the Dharma-realm; the wisdom of the center and periphery within the Dharma-realm; the wisdom that the measure of all worlds is equal to the Dharma-realm; the wisdom that illuminates and examines all worlds; the wisdom that brings all sentient beings to fulfillment; the wisdom of all phenomena; and the boundless wisdom of the Buddhas—because this Bodhisattva dwells in the wisdom of all Buddhas.
Why is this? It is because one has heard such wisdom regarding the principle of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*).
O Son of the Buddha!
Therefore, this is called the Bodhisattva’s Stage of Empowerment (Abhiṣeka-vihāra).
*The Great Vaipulya Sūtra of the Jewel Radiance of Dhāraṇī*, Scroll One.
*The Great Vaipulya Sūtra of the Jewel Radiance of Dhāraṇī*, Scroll Two.
Translated by the Imperial Edict by the Tripitaka Master and State Preceptor, the Saṃgha-member of Purple Robes, Fǎtiān, of Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India, Western Heaven.

At that time, after the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Dharmamati had expounded these ten stages of bodhisattva practice for the sake of all bodhisattvas, then, through the supernatural power of the Buddha, in each of the ten directions there were worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten thousand buddha-fields; in each of those worlds, as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field, the earth shook in six ways.

That is to say: it shook, shook everywhere, and shook equally everywhere; it quaked, quaked everywhere, and quaked equally everywhere; it crashed, crashed everywhere, and crashed equally everywhere; it surged, surged everywhere, and surged equally everywhere; it roared, roared everywhere, and roared equally everywhere; it rose, rose everywhere, and rose equally everywhere.

At that time, through the supernatural power of the Buddha, there rained down clouds of various celestial flowers, clouds of various celestial incenses, clouds of various celestial unguents, clouds of various celestial garlands, clouds of various celestial powdered incenses, clouds of various celestial robes, clouds of various celestial parasols, clouds of various celestial jewels, clouds of various celestial exquisite lotuses, clouds of various celestial necklaces, and clouds of various celestial ornaments; such diverse clouds of offerings rained down, pervading the surroundings on all sides.

Furthermore, various kinds of celestial and exquisite music, unstruck yet spontaneously resonating in the void, produced great sounds; their brilliant light shone forth, pervading the four great continents, surpassing the Iron Ring Mountains, and extending throughout the ten directions, universally making offerings.

When the Bodhisattva Dharmamati preached this Dharma, throughout all worlds in the ten directions, this same Dharma of the Ten Abodes was simultaneously being taught; even down to the words, phrases, and meanings, they were neither increased nor diminished, but were entirely identical.

Furthermore, by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, from each of the worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten thousand buddha-fields, there gathered from the ten directions bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within ten thousand buddha-fields, who came and addressed the Bodhisattva Dharmamati, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!
Excellent, excellent!
Son of the Buddha!
It is just as you have described the ten stages of the bodhisattva. Son of the Buddha!
They share my name, and their teaching of the Dharma is likewise the same.
All such Bodhisattvas named Dharmamati have come here from the presence of all the Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions.

By the majestic power of the Buddha, in that World of Dharma-Clouds, this wheel of Dharma is turned simultaneously in all places; thus, its various natures, characteristics, words, and meanings neither increase nor decrease.
"O Son of the Buddha!

At that time, through the majestic power of the Buddha, the entire assembly saw that multitude arrive here just as I have arrived in this world; likewise, from all the worlds of the ten directions, within the palaces of Śakra atop Mount Sumeru in all the four great continents, bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten thousand buddha-fields also gathered together."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Dharmamati, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, surveyed the assemblies throughout the dharma-realms of the ten directions. Desiring to restate this meaning, he spoke these verses:

"Beholding the pure wisdom of all Tathāgatas, And their towering power of transformation such as this, Adorned with the multitude of merits of the Ten Powers— For this reason, I have resolved upon this bodhicitta."
Beholding these various supernormal powers, And the preaching of the Dharma that benefits all sentient beings,
Furthermore seeing the various sufferings of saṃsāra, I have therefore resolved upon this bodhicitta;
Before this Tathāgata Samantabhadra, I have heard of the ocean of all merits.
Because it is like space, devoid of marks, one therefore gives rise to this bodhicitta;
Because all abodes and places of birth, and each of their individual natures and behaviors,
are clearly understood through the pursuit of the wisdom that discerns their respective differences, one therefore gives rise to this bodhicitta.
At this time, all the good and evil of the past and present, and even that of the future, are well-cultivated for the sake of seeking this wisdom; therefore, one gives rise to this bodhicitta.
It is likewise with meditative concentration, liberation, samādhi, and the purity of samāpatti.
Out of reverence for this wisdom, one seeks it; therefore, one generates this bodhicitta.
Possessing the power of the faculties throughout all worlds, which are as they are, serene, pure, and equal— Seeking this wisdom, one trains in its meaning; therefore, one generates this bodhicitta.
Enlightenment and liberation pervade the world, Within which there are various and diverse intentions;
To seek this wisdom, countless treatises have been composed, And for this reason, one generates this bodhicitta.
Within the various and countless realms of the triple world, There further exist various distinct elements (*dhātu*).
One should seek the wisdom of the intrinsic nature of the elements; therefore, one generates this bodhicitta.
Seeking this Dharma by traveling everywhere, one relies upon it thus to attain peace and happiness;
understanding the true nature of reality, one generates this bodhicitta.
Arising within all lands, just as sentient beings exist by depending upon the earth, those with countless eyes of wisdom seek it in this same way; for this reason, they give rise to this bodhicitta.
Regarding the various natures and characteristics of sentient beings in the past, present, and future—
Thus knowing all past events, they therefore give rise to this bodhicitta;
Accumulating sentient beings to fill the world, even approaching each one individually,
Thus being able to fully know the exhaustion of their afflictions, they therefore give rise to this bodhicitta.
They know all the wisdom of the three realms and are able to understand the inexhaustible Dharma-gates;
seeking such true and authentic wisdom, they therefore give rise to this bodhicitta.
All phenomena have no dependence; their original nature is like space and free from attachment.
To seek the knowledge of ultimate reality, I therefore generate this bodhicitta;
To shake as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms, And to cause the rivers and seas to surge and boil,
In order to seek such wisdom as the Tathāgata’s, I therefore generate this bodhicitta.
Universally emitting light that illuminates the ten directions, Each ray of light issues forth from the mouth;
Seeking that single wisdom-light, For this reason, I resolve upon this bodhicitta.
In inconceivable and manifold lands, Providing food, drink, and precious playthings—
May my vows also be fully endowed with such wisdom; for this reason, I give rise to this bodhicitta.
May all sentient beings and all buddha-fields be led to stay far away from harming and killing;
seeking this Dharma so that life may be long and enduring, for this reason, I give rise to this bodhicitta.
Even if one were able to know the number of drops from a single hair-tip within all the waters of the great oceans, such wisdom as this I vow to seek; for this reason, I give rise to this bodhicitta.
Regarding all the lands throughout the ten directions, within each and every land, as numerous as the atoms of dust—
Thus, this wisdom must be fully known; for this reason, one generates this bodhicitta.
Regarding all kalpas of the past and the future, and all worlds of the present— one must fully know the number of such kalpas; for this reason, one generates this bodhicitta.
All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, As well as śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas— They fully know the intrinsic nature of all phenomena; Therefore, they give rise to this bodhicitta.
Infinite and countless worlds, Are all weighed and measured within a single hair-tip.
One can fully know the intrinsic nature of all natures; for this reason, one generates this bodhicitta.
The inconceivable world-systems of the Cakravāḍa mountains could be weighed entirely upon the tip of a single hair;
for the sake of such vast and subtle knowledge, one generates this bodhicitta.
Throughout immeasurable and countless worlds, my voice shall pervade them in a single instant;
seeking this pure sound of wisdom, I therefore give rise to this bodhicitta.
All the languages of every world, I shall expound from a single syllable, leaving nothing unsaid.
To realize this true nature of selfhood, I therefore give rise to this bodhicitta;
To guide and transform countless beings throughout the three realms, and to protect all sentient beings, I therefore give rise to this bodhicitta;
To seek the vast tongue of eloquent speech, I therefore give rise to this bodhicitta.
As it is said: "One can see all Buddha-fields within a single kṣaṇa;
seeking the unimpeded wisdom of preaching the Dharma, one thus gives rise to this bodhicitta.
All the fields of the Tathāgatas are completely pervaded within a single kṣaṇa."
Knowing the true nature of the Buddha-dharma in this way, I therefore give rise to this bodhicitta;
Countless worlds, as numerous as motes of dust, All arise from their own intrinsic nature;
Seeking such manifold wisdom, I therefore give rise to this bodhicitta.
The Buddhas of the past and the future, And all those in the worlds of the present— In a single instant, they know them all within their hearts; Therefore, they give rise to this bodhicitta.
A single phrase they speak is inconceivable; Though such eons may end, it remains inexhaustible.
In order to seek such knowledge of language, I therefore give rise to this bodhicitta;
Throughout all the worlds of the eight directions, such a continuity remains unbroken;
in order to understand this through the nature of mind, I therefore give rise to this bodhicitta.
All the three karmas of body, speech, and mind, I perform as all the practices of the ten directions;
Because of this, I can realize the emptiness of the three periods of time, And for this reason, I give rise to this bodhicitta.
One should generate the bodhicitta in this manner, reverently and most supremely honoring all Buddhas;
practicing thus throughout the countless eons of the ten directions, one’s heart of respect shall never regress.
Even toward all those honored within the world, throughout each of the eight directions, [one should act] with universal pervasiveness.
Thus all those Buddhas preach the Dharma, and with a mind of singular respect,
he does not regress; if even a single bodhisattva attains peace and happiness,
by practicing that path he escapes saṃsāra and can manifest the perfect marks of the world— therefore, this Honored One’s mind does not regress.

The most supreme and wondrous Dharma is most extraordinary; Profoundly deep, difficult to understand, and beyond verbal expression, Those Bodhisattvas skillfully proclaim it, Out of reverence for that Honored One, their minds never regressing;
Unshakable in the world and its abodes— Such as this is difficult to attain and exceedingly rare.
He proclaims the pure and wondrous sound of the Dharma; for this reason, the mind of this Honored One does not regress.
Having been born among all Tathāgatas, he is without self or person and free from pride;
seeking this Dharma, he always stands at the forefront—for this reason, his earnest mind does not regress.
Countless, peerless, and incalculable, they attain the samādhis of all Tathāgatas;
practicing such conduct as that of the Bodhisattvas, their minds thus remain diligent and non-regressive.
Until they reach the ultimate samādhi, they transcend birth and understand the further shore.
Thus he speaks of those Buddhas' teachings; for this reason, the mind of this Honored One does not regress.
Having distanced himself from saṃsāra within the three realms, he turns such a wondrous wheel of Dharma, constantly and without interruption throughout all worlds; thus should the bodhisattva speak.
Amidst all the sufferings and afflictions of the world, within such turbid and evil calamities,
out of compassion for all sentient beings, the Bodhisattva should therefore speak.
When the Bodhisattva first expounds this Dharma, Thereby giving rise to the bodhicitta;
Holding the precepts and preaching the Dharma without ceasing, Therefore, it is called the Stage of Generating the Mind (Cittotpāda-vihāra).
At that time, the Bodhisattva dwells in the stage of "Purifying the Ground," first subduing such a mind as this:
to bring peace, happiness, and benefit to the world, just as the Buddha has transcended old age, sickness, and death;
with a mind of faith, a mind of mindfulness, and diligence; and with a mind of wisdom, a mind of aspiration, and the observance of precepts.
Protecting the Dharma, one abandons [the notions of] coming and going; One resolutely dedicates [merit] to all sentient beings.
If one abides in such a mind, Reading, reciting, and upholding the Mahāyāna scriptures, Staying far from clamor in a quiet and secluded place, And seeking out all virtuous and spiritual friends—
Through virtuous speech, one draws near to spiritual friends, Diligently seeking such true and authentic wisdom.
One thoroughly understands all languages, And the principle of ultimate truth is likewise so.
Having clearly realized the ultimate truth of the Tathāgata, One is free from all perversions and devoid of doubt.
Thus, abiding in equanimity and profound stillness, one is called a true son of the Buddha who preaches the Dharma.

Having attained this within the stage of "Cultivating the Ground," one is well able to observe all bodhisattvas, expounding the wondrous Dharma and honoring all Buddhas; therefore, sons of the Buddha should train themselves accordingly.
Furthermore, in the third dwelling of the Bodhisattva, One seeks the practice of Buddhahood within the teaching of the Dharma King;
One fully understands suffering, emptiness, and impermanence, And that all intrinsic natures have neither coming nor going.
All phenomena are fundamentally quiescent and devoid of intrinsic nature; With a mind of certain realization, one clearly and thoroughly penetrates them.
Abiding herein, they are entirely free from delusion; The Son of the Buddha should speak thus:
To know the realms of all sentient beings, And to elucidate all realms of phenomena— Thus knowing these worlds in their entirety, Therefore it is called "corresponding practice."
The earth element, the water element, and the fire element, as well as the wind element and the space element;
the realm of desire, the realm of form, and the formless realm—all these worlds he knows completely, even down to their various distinctions.
He perceives the essential nature of the dharma-realm itself.
Thus, this Honored One of Vast Wisdom, with courageous diligence, seeks the Buddha-knowledge.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dwells in the Stage of Noble Birth; having left the household life, he is born among all Tathāgatas.
With certainty regarding the nature of existence and non-existence, wherever he is born, his vision is always correct.
The Bodhisattvas on this stage are non-regressive; seeking the Buddha-way, their minds never weary.
They constantly cultivate all dharmas and regard all sentient beings as their own nature.
The myriad sins of the world are like motes of dust across the lands;
Far removed from the various retributions of saṃsāra, The sons of the Buddha skillfully discern their arising, And cause all bodhisattvas to be free from decay and old age.
Regarding all phenomena of the past, present, and future, their wisdom is perfectly clear;
having planted roots of goodness with virtuous friends in former lives, they are all born together, just as when a Buddha appears in the world.

All Tathāgatas are most excellent and sublime; Entering the equanimous mind of the three times, They are able to produce such supreme and wondrous births, Transcending the various activities of the three times.
This is called the fourth bodhisattva dwelling; he is able to praise this sublime form.
He can fully understand and realize these dharmas, awakening to the birth of the bodhisattva in such a manner.
Thereafter, the Bodhisattva is called the fifth, And is said to dwell in the perfection of skillful means (*upāya*).
Through various skillful means he transforms all living beings; Delighting in seeking meritorious deeds, he travels everywhere.
The vast merit thus performed Causes all sentient beings to attain liberation.
Dedicating with all one's heart, may all obtain peace; out of compassion for sentient beings, may they be freed from bondage.
May all the world’s afflictions and hardships be rescued and relieved, and may they be subdued so that joy arises within them.
May each and every sentient being be guided toward the attainment of Great Nirvana and the tranquility of mind.
The boundless entirety of all worlds— thus immeasurable and innumerable,
transcending all calculation and peerless— is neither a nature, nor a characteristic, nor an ultimate.
This is the fifth dwelling of the Bodhisattva, Fully endowed with skillful means to transform all living beings;
That Buddha, thus wondrous, perfect, and luminous, Manifests all manner of meritorious virtues.

All infinite sentient beings, observing the self-nature of phenomena without delusion, understand through wisdom the net of doubt regarding existence and non-existence; they are steadfast in both the heavens and the human realm.
Toward the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Bodhisattvas, they constantly practice sublime conduct, remaining free from all [worldly] forms;
toward these vast multitudes of sentient beings, they listen to and proclaim the teachings of skillful means.
They purify sentient beings afflicted by defilements, Subduing those easy to transform and those difficult to tame;
Whether the Dharma-realm is vast or concise, they proclaim it. Neither coming nor going, they are free from all marks;
The essence of the Dharma-realm is neither existent nor non-existent— Bodhisattvas joyfully listen to and receive this throughout the three periods of time.
Observing that all minds are without movement, one thus focuses single-mindedly on the Buddha-dharma.
When nature and characteristics are extinguished, who can say there is existence or non-existence? My own nature is likewise free from defilement;
understanding that the nature of kalpas is like an illusion or a dream, I have come to hear this most sublime Dharma.

A non-retrogressive bodhisattva should act thus: regarding the Buddha, the Dharma, and the assembly of bodhisattvas, as well as observing their characteristics as being existent or non-existent, they realize that non-retrogression is neither existent nor non-existent.
The Tathāgata neither departs nor abides; He neither comes nor does he not come.
Birth and non-birth, exhaustion and non-exhaustion, The presence of marks and the absence of marks are neither one nor different.
Though manifold and diverse, they are as one; The principle of ultimate truth is free from existence and non-existence.
Each adorned with various distinct jewels, the Bodhisattva’s mind does not regress therein.
The wondrous marks of True Suchness (tathatā) are neither existent nor non-existent; through the wisdom of signlessness (animitta-jñāna), one can understand them.
Thus, amidst these differences, they proceed to the assemblies, hearing [the Dharma] upon every single celestial realm.
Furthermore, when a Bodhisattva dwells in the stage of youthful innocence, their physical, verbal, and mental actions are entirely pure;

they perform Buddha-works without attachment. Therefore, wherever they are born according to their will, it arises from the practice of the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings; they travel and behold all those buddha-fields.
Wisdom is swiftly attained according to one’s wish; from the ten directions, all pay homage with earnest reverence.

The Bodhisattva remains free from any dualistic mind herein; hearing the Buddha expound the subtle and wondrous Dharma, they are able to know that all lands tremble, knowing this exhaustively without exception.
They travel and preach throughout the Buddha-fields, reaching an asankhyeya of them in a single kṣaṇa;
they expound countless meanings according to questions, and likewise regarding their essential natures and specific distinctions.
Through the sounds of skillful means, they are able to illuminate and examine countless Buddha-fields within a single thought-moment.
Furthermore, it is said that the Bodhisattva dwells as a prince; his secret conduct is beyond the measurement of sentient beings.
With the barriers of affliction closed and delusive thoughts eliminated, he teaches through skillful means in accord with both phenomena and principle.
He is able to perform all manner of wondrous practices and discerns the worlds of the past and the future.
Able to thoroughly understand the two truths of the ultimate and the conventional, they seek such subtle and wondrous Dharma.
Skillfully employing expedient means, they enter the royal city; thus they travel everywhere throughout its entirety.
They possess mastery over coming and going therein, and are able to clearly observe all within the royal city.
Just as the sublime Dharma is like a consecrated king, so too is the power of its majesty;
entering that royal city, he expounds it skillfully—therefore, this is called the Dwelling of the Prince.
This one can accord with all sentient beings; just as the Buddha’s emanations are, so too is this one.
The appearance of the Tamer is entirely the same; having attained the peace of a Buddha, he dwells as a prince.
The Buddha-sons dwelling in the Bodhisattva stage of Consecration, Abiding in the supreme and foremost state, are able to benefit others;
Even if one were to measure them by drops of water from a single hair, Their contemplation and calculation could not fathom them.

Thus one practices the teachings of all Buddhas; though all the lands of atoms may be known by sentient beings, yet no one can fathom the atoms themselves—therefore, it must be described as being beyond measure.
All Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas, together with the Buddhas of the past and future,
as well as those currently in the ten directions— including Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas—
who have given rise to the bodhicitta from their seeds: such a number is impossible to measure.
The measure of its merit cannot be known; from that very first thought of bodhicitta, it transforms sentient beings throughout such worlds—none can surpass or exceed it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed the Bodhisattva Dharmamati, saying: "Noble son!
Excellent, excellent!"
"You have now well expounded this Dharma-gate of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, son of good family!
Those sentient beings shall attain love and joy for the inconceivable merits of all Buddhas and for all-encompassing wisdom."

"Good son! If there are sentient beings who merely hear the name of this True Dharma, the Treasure-Light Dhāraṇī, they need not maintain, read, or recite it; by revering it with single-minded devotion, they will ultimately and certainly attain the fruit of Buddhahood."
Then the Bodhisattva Dharmamati said:
"O Son of the Buddha! So it is, so it is!"
"It is as you have said.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said:
"O Son of the Buddha!

They have already attained the profound wisdom of the Tathāgata’s empowerment. If there are sons or daughters of good family who, having come to this assembly, hear such a Dharma as this; or if there are sentient beings who hold this sutra in their hands—all such beings shall receive a prediction of enlightenment within the Buddha-dharma.
At that time, the Elder Śāriputra rose from his seat, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We are now like those born blind; since the distant past, we have never before seen or heard such a true Dharma.”
World-Honored One!
It is not only for my sake; if all sentient beings do not hear this Dharma, then all such sentient beings as these would likewise be like those born blind.
The Buddha said: "Elder! So it is, so it is!"
"It is as you have said.
Śāriputra then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I only pray that You will speak this inconceivable and profound Dharma."
The Buddha said,
“Śāriputra, you should go and summon that Brahmā King, Śakra, and the world-protecting devas to come together to this assembly.”
The Tathāgata commanded Śāriputra:
"This most excellent Dharma-seal, the Jewel-Light Dhāraṇī, was taught by me in that assembly at the site of enlightenment."

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, having received the Buddha’s instruction to inquire after this Dharma-gate of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī, and bearing the Buddha’s sacred mandate, went to those Brahma kings, Śakras, and world-protecting devas.

Upon arrival, he spoke these words: “The Buddha awaits your coming at the Jewel Light Bodhimaṇḍa; you shall hear and receive this Dharma together. Now is the very moment, for the Tathāgata is about to preach this inconceivable Dharma of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī. You must assemble quickly and do not let this opportunity pass; such an encounter is extremely difficult to find, and you will surely regret it later.”
"Such a most supreme jewel of the Dharma is difficult to find in the world; it is exceedingly rare.

When those devas heard these words, they immediately exercised their supernatural powers, and in a single kṣaṇa, Brahmā, Śakra, and the world-protecting devas all assembled. Arriving at the place where the World-Honored One was, they circumambulated him three times to the right, joined their palms in reverence, and stood before the Buddha, entreating the World-Honored One:
"We pray only that the Tathāgata, out of compassion for us and for the sentient beings of the final dharma age, will preach this Dharma-gate of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī."
At that time, the World-Honored One remained silent and did not answer.
Then the assembly of devas, Brahmā, Śakra, and the world-protecting devas made this request three times with earnest entreaty, yet the World-Honored One remained silent.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"I only pray that the Tathāgata will preach this Dharma of the Jewel Radiance Dhāraṇī.
He spoke again:
“Sugata! We only pray that you will speak of it.
At that time, the World-Honored One produced various sounds from his tongue-organ, which issued forth from his mouth and pervaded the trichiliocosm, so that they were heard simultaneously throughout.
"If there are good sons who, for the sake of this Jewel Light Dhāraṇī Dharma, invite the Tathāgata, all those sentient beings shall attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: "Venerable Śāriputra!
You should go to invite the youth Mañjuśrī."

While this Dharma was being taught, the youth Mañjuśrī was in another place, beneath a *bhallātakī* śāla tree, sitting cross-legged with body erect and right mindfulness, surpassing the light of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of suns and moons. He dwelt within a great pavilion adorned with jewels, surrounded by and revered by Brahmā kings, Śakras, and world-protecting devas; their bodies were all golden, adorned with auspiciousness, and radiantly luminous.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, having received the Buddha’s command, went to the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was; upon arrival, he addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
“O son of good family!
"The Tathāgata requests that you, for our sake, explain this Dharma of the Jewel-Light Dhāraṇī.
At that time, the Youth Mañjuśrī addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:
"In what sense is he called 'the Tathāgata'?"
Śāriputra said: "Good son! Your wisdom is profound and far-reaching;
I am not of your caliber, and for this reason I am not fit to engage in debate with you."
Mañjuśrī said: "Stop, Śāriputra!"
"You are extremely ignorant; if you would like to hear it, I shall explain it for you. Śāriputra said, "Good man!..."
"I now wish to hear it; I only pray that you, O Benevolent One, will explain it extensively for me.

At that time, as the youth Mañjuśrī spoke these words, immediately the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system, including the pure celestial palaces and the hosts of devas, up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven—
The hosts of *ḍāka* deities, down to the Four Great Heavenly Kings and their innumerable *koṭi* of yakṣa retinues,
along with the Brahmā kings, Śakra the Lord of Devas, the world-protecting devas,
and various celestial maidens— each desiring to hear such a great Dharma— all assembled together, as did the bhikṣus and...
Bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, as well as the other devas of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven,
Yāma heaven, Tuṣita heaven, Nirmāṇarati heaven, Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven,
Mahābrahmā, and Akaniṣṭha heaven— all such hosts of devas came together for this assembly.
Furthermore, there was an assembly of great śrāvakas, whose names were: the Venerable Subhūti,
the Venerable Mahākāśyapa, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana, the Venerable Śāriputra, the Venerable Mahākātyāyana, the Venerable Aniruddha, and the Venerable Gayākāśyapa.
...the Venerable Mahākauṣṭhila, the Venerable Śaṇavāsa, the Venerable Revata,
the Venerable Nadīkāśyapa, the Venerable Uruvilvākāśyapa, the Venerable Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra, the Venerable Rāhula, and the Venerable Bakkula.
Rāhula, the Venerable Māṣpaka, the Venerable Ānanda,
and other such great śrāvakas, as well as Yaśodharā and five hundred bhikṣuṇīs,
all gathered together.
Furthermore, there were wheel-turning kings and various minor kings, kṣatriyas, brahmins, elders, and householders, all of whom came to assemble.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra circumambulated the Buddha three times and spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!
“For what cause and for what reason have such a great assembly gathered here this very day?
How should we understand this?
The Buddha said:
“Venerable Śāriputra! This is due to the majestic power of the Dharma of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī. Śāriputra said:
“World-Honored One!
I now wish to hear this Dharma-gate of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī.
The Buddha said:
“Venerable Śāriputra!
You should go and request Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; these two Great Beings will surely explain it for you.”
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the youth Mañjuśrī, saying: "Noble son,
you should now expound this subtle and wondrous Dharma-jewel of the Jewel Light Samādhi."
Mañjuśrī said: "Venerable Śāriputra!
You and the others now wish to hear this dhāraṇī of the Jewel Light."
Śāriputra said: "The fourfold assembly here, as well as Brahmā, Śakra, and the world-protecting devas, have come to this place in order to hear this Dharma."
At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the Elder Śāriputra, saying: "Śāriputra!
This secret essence of the Dharma cannot be seen or heard; it is like an illusion and like a transformation. How, then, can it be explained?"
"Who is it that speaks and listens? Śāriputra replied,
"O son of good family!"
"You should now speak; I wish to hear it with joy.
Mañjuśrī asked the Venerable Śāriputra:
"How should this teaching be expressed?"
He replied: "Mañjuśrī, you speak thus in vain."
Mañjuśrī asked Śāriputra again:
"How do you speak of emptiness? He replied:
“Mañjuśrī, emptiness is beyond verbal expression. Mañjuśrī replied:
"Venerable Śāriputra! If this emptiness were beyond verbal expression, how could I speak of it?
Venerable Śāriputra!"
"Since all dharmas are entirely beyond verbal expression, if one were to speak thus,
who could listen and receive it? The Elder Śāriputra said, "Good son!"

Because all those phenomena are free from letters and language, it is thus said: they are empty, signless, wishless; neither grasped nor abandoned; neither different nor not different; neither free from conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) nor not free from conceptual proliferation.

At that time, when the youth Mañjuśrī and the Venerable Śāriputra had spoken this Dharma, those bodhisattvas, as well as the Brahmā kings, Śakra, and the world-protecting devas, were filled with great joy and praised them in unison, saying: "Excellent!"
"Noble son! It is because you have well expounded this Dharma of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the youth Mañjuśrī, saying:
“Good son! How does a bodhisattva-mahāsattva receive, uphold, read, recite, and explain to others this Dharma of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī? Mañjuśrī replied:

“Subhūti! This dharma of dhāraṇī is unborn and pure; one should receive and uphold it according to the principle, free from intrinsic nature and free from marks, neither departing from verbal expression, nor grasping, nor abandoning.”
"This Dharma should be received and upheld in this manner, and explained to others.

When the youth Mañjuśrī-kumārabhūta spoke these words, ninety-two bodhisattvas all attained the *vīrya-samādhi*, and furthermore, sixty-two beings among gods and humans attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
"What is the great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
The Buddha said: "Good son!..."
Regarding this great compassion of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not abandon the triple world, it is called great compassion;
if they cause all sentient beings to behold the pure and wondrous buddha-fields, it is called great compassion;
if they are able to feel pity for and protect all sentient beings who have broken the precepts, it is called great compassion.
If one can cause all sentient beings to aspire to and personally cultivate the *prajñāpāramitā*, this is called great compassion;
if, for the sake of all sentient beings, one does not begrudge even body or life, this is called great compassion;

and if, for the sake of all sentient beings, one is able to relinquish what is difficult to relinquish—even head, eyes, marrow, and brain—and perform what is difficult to perform, this is called great compassion.
Again he addressed them, saying: "Good sons!

For the sake of all sentient beings, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas maintain no dualistic mind; they bestow peace and happiness equally, free them from all false views, and cause them all to attain liberation."
