“Good son! This is the great compassion of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; you should understand it in this way.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

We only pray that the Tathāgata, with immeasurable great compassion, for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings and the world, will preach this Dharma of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī; thereby, all those in this great assembly—both devas and humans—shall obtain peace, happiness, and benefit.”
Immediately, the World-Honored One, out of compassion for all sentient beings, addressed all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas with a Brahma-voice, saying:
"In the future age, during the final five hundred years when the Dharma is about to perish, who among you will be able to receive, uphold, and widely proclaim this Dharma of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī?"
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin Bodhisattva, Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva, Pratibhānasaṃbhava Bodhisattva,
Sarvadharmotpādavikrāmin Bodhisattva, Akṣayamati Bodhisattva, Sāgaramati Bodhisattva,
Ratnasiṃha Bodhisattva, Ratnabhadra Bodhisattva, and Ratnaprabha Bodhisattva— [and so forth].
[Sarva-]śūra, Ratna-cūḍa Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Samantadarśin Bodhisattva, Nityadarśin Bodhisattva,
Ratnapāṇi Bodhisattva, Ratnakūṭa Bodhisattva, Ratnavyūha Bodhisattva, Śrīdhvaja Bodhisattva,
Dharmalakṣmī Bodhisattva, Lakṣmī-dhana Bodhisattva, Puṇyalakṣmī [Bodhisattva].
The Bodhisattva Śrī, the Bodhisattva Candanaśrī, the Bodhisattva Dharmamati, the Bodhisattva Amṛtamati, the Bodhisattva Acintya, the Bodhisattva Puṇyavyūha, the Bodhisattva Guṇavyūha,
the Bodhisattva Lakṣaṇavyūha, the Bodhisattva Nityapramuditendriya, and the Bodhisattva Sarvajñānakūṭarāja.
Sattva, Prajñākūṭa Bodhisattva, Nityotkṣiptahasta Bodhisattva, Dharaṇīdhara Bodhisattva, Mativikrama Bodhisattva, Gaganagañja Bodhisattva, Candragarbha Bodhisattva,
Vimalacandragarbha Bodhisattva, Sūryagarbha Bodhisattva, Janmarāja Bodhisattva, Mahāmeru Bodhisattva, Dṛḍha... [Bodhisattva].
The Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya,
and these sixty-two hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, with a single voice, spoke simultaneously:
“World-Honored One!

We are now able, in the future age during the final five hundred years when the Dharma is about to perish, to constantly receive, uphold, widely proclaim, and disseminate this *Ratnaprabhāsa-dhāraṇī* dharma-gate for the sake of all sentient beings.”
The Buddha said: “Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!”
Rare, rare indeed! Sons of good family,
for the sake of all sentient beings, you are able to give rise to such pure and great vows.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, saying:
"Listen attentively!
Listen attentively!"
"Good son, this subtle and wondrous True Dharma of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī is intended to benefit, bring peace, and provide happiness to all sentient beings.
At that time, having spoken these words, the World-Honored One ascended the lion throne adorned with great jewels, sat in the full lotus posture, and then spoke the Jewel Radiance Dhāraṇī:

*Namo bhagavate sarvathā mahe sarvathā mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā oṃ vara-vare vara-vare vara-vare ti svāhā.* At that time, the World-Honored One thus recited this Dharma-treasure of the Jewel-Light Dhāraṇī—secret, subtle, most supreme, profoundly deep, and vast—three times.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Regarding ‘dharmas’ and ‘that which possesses dharmas,’ what is the meaning of this?”

The Buddha said: “Good son! The non-existence of dharmas is itself dharma; it is the meaning of all things, the meaning of the absence of intrinsic nature. The meaning of all dharmas is the meaning of being equal to empty space. All dharmas are the meaning of the incalculable; the meaning of the incalculable is the meaning of all things; the meaning of the incalculable is the meaning of all dharmas.”
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how do you explain all these dharmas?”
The Buddha said, “Good son!
When I speak of all these dharmas, I refer to the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; likewise, these six consciousnesses and the twelve links of dependent origination.”
"Good son! For this reason, because I have now made this statement, all dharmas are likewise so.
Furthermore, good son!"
"All dharmas are fundamentally without arising or ceasing.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, saying these words:
"O Son of the Buddha!"
"How should a bodhisattva receive and uphold this Dharma-gate of the Jewel Light Dhāraṇī?
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
"O son of good family!..."
This Jewel Light Dhāraṇī is spoken according to the Dharma and should be received and upheld in accordance with reality.

Why? Because its fundamental nature is neither born nor extinguished; because it is neither a characteristic nor empty; because the absence of nature is itself the self-nature; and because the self-nature is itself the absence of nature.

"Noble son! This Jewel Light Dhāraṇī is such that one should not be attached to it; because one upholds, receives, and contemplates it, one should abide in and explain it through the definitive understanding of wisdom."
"Good son! This is because the dhāraṇī of jewel-light contemplates the meaning of the self-nature of phenomena.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master and Imperial Preceptor of the Teaching, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject Fǎtiān, at Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India, in the Western Heavens.
Translated by Imperial Decree. At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Youth Mañjuśrī, saying:
"Noble son, for how long will this sublime Dharma remain in the world?"
Mañjuśrī said: “Śāriputra, it is because of these three poisons: greed, hatred, and delusion.”
Śāriputra said: "Good son! For how long do this greed, hatred, and delusion abide?"
Mañjuśrī said: “Śāriputra,
these three poisons abide because they are like the element of earth.”
Śāriputra said: “Good son, upon how much further does this earth element abide?”
Mañjuśrī said: “Śāriputra!
These three poisons and the earth element are like the element of ignorance.”
Śāriputra said: “Good son! For how long do this ignorance and the three poisons abide?”
Mañjuśrī said: “Śāriputra, it is because it is like the realm of space.”
Śāriputra said: "Good son! For how long will these three poisons abide within the realm of empty space?"
Mañjuśrī said: “Śāriputra, it is because dharmas have the nature of being without intrinsic nature.”
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed Mañjuśrī, saying: "Noble son!
Since your wisdom and eloquence are such as this, how could I possess the power of wisdom to engage in debate with you?"
Furthermore, good son!
It is like all the cats and wildcats in the world treading upon Mount Sumeru; they could never exhaust it. Just so, just so!
"Good son! We are also like this, just like those cats and wildcats. Why is that?"
Just as all the śrāvakas together cannot ultimately defeat a single bodhisattva in debate, how much less could they do so against this Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta?
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed the youth Mañjuśrī, saying: “Good son!

You have now questioned the Tathāgata, saying to the World-Honored One: ‘In the future age, during the final five hundred years, how shall that Dharma King, the Jewel Radiance Dhāraṇī, be protected and upheld?’”
"How does the Dharma-preacher who upholds this sutra show compassion so that [beings] may attain firmness?
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī rose calmly from his own Dharma-seat and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
“If there is a Dharma master who receives, maintains, reads, recites, and explains this True Dharma for others,
what merit will they obtain? The Buddha said, “Mañjuśrī!”

If there be any bhikṣu who upholds this King of Dharmas, because he shall be born into the pure Dharma-body and because he shall attain ultimate Buddha-enlightenment, he will thus constantly abide within the teachings of all Buddhas during the interim, his mind never regressing; neither any celestial Māras nor their retinues shall be able to afflict or disturb him.

If there is a son of good family who, for even a mere snap of the fingers, gives rise to a thought of loving-kindness toward that Dharma teacher, that person shall immediately transcend saṃsāra and ultimately attain the Bodhi of a Buddha.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī!

If one who upholds this Dharma King of Jewel Radiance gives rise to a mind of contempt or slander, that person will, in life after life, have teeth that are sparse and missing, a flat nose, and no tongue; their hands and feet will be withered and crippled; they will suffer from chronic and grave illnesses; they will be dull-witted, foolish, blind, and deaf; they will be born into low and base circumstances, and be indolent and lazy.
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
"Such deluded sentient beings as these— I shall now briefly describe them for you, noble son."
After those beings have passed away, they undergo countless hells, as numerous as the hairs on a single pore, experiencing various kinds of suffering and affliction.
