A single thought of resolve gives birth to the Buddha-dharma;
having thus generated the mind through such harmony, he does not seek the pleasures of kingship, nor personal security, nor fame and profit.
To extinguish all the sufferings and afflictions of the world, he enters the world for the sake of the minds of all beings.
His mind is ever for the sake of all sentient beings; he purifies Buddha-fields and offers worship.
By practicing this Dharma, he realizes Bodhi, and from his mind arises pure wisdom.
He constantly reveres and seeks liberation; he respects all living beings with the perception of them as Buddhas.
Since the merit of all dharmas is equal, he gives rise to such a mind and remains ever respectful.
Having resolved to take refuge in the Buddha-dharma, the sons of the Buddha give rise to the mind and practice this conduct;
at that moment, boundless bodhi is generated, and the courageous and sharp resolve of a great man is born.

The power of the resolve is like that of a sovereign among men; Extensively performing inconceivable offerings, Such that all dharmas are indestructible and immeasurable— One should generate the mind for offering in this manner.
The aspiration for enlightenment can avoid the suffering of the womb; it brings to an end all acts of laborious nurturing and rearing.
All joys follow one’s heart as desired; therefore, one beholds a state of peace and bliss.
Arousing boundless reverence, I utterly abandon pride regarding self and person;
this arousal of the mind is a wondrous treasure-trove, like holding it in one's hand to obtain peace and happiness.
The resolve can bring about joyful relinquishment; The resolve brings forth exultation for the work of Buddhas;
The resolve seeks the forest of supreme merit; Having attained it, one proceeds everywhere as taught by the Buddhas.
Brave, of sharp faculties, and radiant with light, their resolve is firm and indestructible;
all various afflictions are suddenly eliminated, and they can proclaim the virtues of the Buddha upon generating the mind of enlightenment.
The arising of the mind, whether in harmony or disharmony, is entirely transcended in a single kṣaṇa;
by this arising of the mind, one can cross beyond the realm of the Māra King and behold that most supreme and wondrous liberation.
The seeds of merit are the cause of imperishability; by generating the aspiration, one plants the great Bodhi tree.
Supreme and victorious wisdom increases in every way, and through the generation of the aspiration, one beholds all Buddhas.
He speaks of those who practiced great deeds in the past, seeking liberation through sublime conduct by generating the resolve for enlightenment;
this Dharma is extremely difficult to encounter in the world, like a sovereign jewel within the great ocean.
If one constantly arouses the mind to revere the Buddha, Though lacking precepts or conduct, they are freed from all such things;
Having abandoned all faults, calamities, and transgressions, They are further able to praise his meritorious virtues.
Maintaining the precepts gives rise to the bodhicitta; through skillful means, one cultivates the stages of merit.
Being able to rely on the dharma of the precepts and practice them well, such a person always follows the instructions and exhortations of the Buddha.
If one constantly arouses the mind to revere the Buddha, that Buddha will extensively receive offerings;
having made extensive offerings to the Buddha, one can further be earnest and inconceivable.
If one constantly resolves to make offerings to the Dharma, hearing that Buddha-Dharma with a mind free from weariness;
if one’s mind never tires of the Buddha-Dharma, one will attain the wondrous liberation of the inconceivable Dharma.
If one constantly arouses the mind to revere the Saṅgha, One’s mind will not regress toward the Saṅgha;
Arousing the mind in this way so that the Saṅgha does not regress, One shall attain the power of non-regression in the arousal of the mind.
If one attains the power of non-retrogression in generating the resolve, they manifest radiance through their sharp faculties;
if they manifest radiance through their sharp faculties, they will always remain far removed from evil associates.
If one has already distanced oneself from evil associates, one should seek the Dharma and visit virtuous friends;
having sought both the Dharma and virtuous friends, one will obtain vast and sublime peace and happiness.
If one attains vast and sublime peace and bliss, one abandons all forms of pride through the power of that cause;
once the cause of pride has been abandoned, one immediately attains vast and supreme liberation.
Having thus attained such vast liberation, one is immediately perceived by all Buddhas;
and being thus constantly perceived by all Buddhas, one gives rise to the great bodhicitta.
If one succeeds in giving rise to the great bodhicitta, One immediately attains the great merit of liberation;
If one attains the great merit of liberation, One immediately takes birth in the family of the Tathāgata.
Having been born into the family of the Tathāgata, one immediately attains the wondrous union of liberation;
if one always maintains this wondrous union of liberation, the intentions of that mind will be entirely pure.
The Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī-ratna-prabhāsa Sūtra, Scroll Three;
The Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī-ratna-prabhāsa Sūtra, Scroll Four.
Translated at Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India, in the Land of the West.
The Tripitaka Master Dengyō, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa and Subject Fǎtiān, says:
“If one can give rise to the mind of pure awakening, that is said to be the most supreme and most excellent;
having attained this most supreme excellence, one should constantly practice the pāramitās.”
If one practices the conduct of the pāramitās, one can accordingly follow this Mahāyāna;
if one can accordingly follow this Mahāyāna, one can accordingly follow in making offerings to the Buddha.
If one attains the opportunity to make offerings in accordance with the Buddha, one will then attain wisdom and firm resolve;
if one can possess wisdom and firm resolve, one will constantly behold that inconceivable Buddha.
If one constantly perceives the Buddha’s inconceivability, One sees that the Buddha neither departs nor abides;
If one attains this vision of the Buddha’s non-departure and non-abiding, This Dharma will abide in the world forever without perishing.
If one sees that this Dharma is eternally indestructible, One remains far removed from the accumulation of all afflictions;
If one attains such removal from the causes of affliction, Then one can preach the Dharma without limit.
If one attains the boundless teaching of the Dharma, one arises with compassion and dwells in the world;
if one dwells in the world with a compassionate mind, that is the firm foundation of great compassion.
If one attains the firm foundation of great compassion, that itself is the joy and delight of the Dharma for others;
if one attains the foundation of the joy and delight of the Dharma, they will abandon the commission of various evils.
If one abandons the commission of manifold transgressions, There is no self and no person, free from all that is erroneous;
If one attains non-self and is free from all that is erroneous, That person will always benefit both themselves and others.
If one constantly benefits oneself and others, one will forever be free from the various sufferings of saṃsāra;
being free from the various sufferings of saṃsāra, one attains great power that is most supreme.
If one attains great power that is most supreme, then one gives birth to pure wisdom;
once pure wisdom has been born, one enters the net of worldly practice.
If one can enter this net of practice, it is most rare to bring the world to maturity;
if one brings the world to maturity, one accumulates the sublime wisdom of the world.
If one attains the sublime wisdom of the world, Then one can accord with the four means of integration;
If one can accord with the four means of integration, Then one extensively establishes them within the world.
If one extensively establishes [teachings] within the world, one abides by the power of skillful means and wisdom;
if one attains the power of skillful means and wisdom, one abides in the courageous, unsurpassed path.
If one dwells in the courageous, unsurpassed path, one will never again behold the hosts of Māra;
having attained the state where the hosts of Māra are no longer seen, one is then able to remain far removed from the four paths of Māra.
If one succeeds in distancing oneself from the paths of the four māras, Then one can reach the stage of non-retrogression;
If one reaches the stage of non-retrogression, Then one is named as having attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
If one attains such patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena, one receives the Buddha’s prediction of enlightenment with the title "Lamp of the World.
Having received this prediction as the "Lamp of the World," one then dwells before all Tathāgatas.
If one dwells before the Tathāgata, one attains the Buddha’s secret wisdom of transformation;
if one attains the Tathāgata’s wisdom of transformation, all Tathāgatas bestow upon one the prediction of enlightenment.
Once one has received the prophecy from all Buddhas, one is adorned with the multitude of all merits;
having attained this adornment of the multitude of merits, one obtains a wondrous, meritorious, and pure body.
If one attains such a pure body, Radiant like the light of a mountain of gold;
If one attains such golden mountain radiance, One shall immediately possess the thirty-two marks.
If one attains the thirty-two marks of perfection, one will immediately attain a body adorned with the primary and secondary marks;
once adorned with these marks, the body emits radiance that shines everywhere.
Once one has attained the light that shines everywhere, adorned by inconceivable multitudes of rays;
having attained such manifold adornments, lotuses arise beneath one’s radiant footsteps.
If one attains the practice of the radiant lotus, One attains the lotus seat of the Buddha’s realm;
Once having attained the Tathāgata’s lotus seat, One is then able to illuminate and perceive the worlds of the ten directions.
If one attains the illumination that perceives the realms of the ten directions, One’s practice of teaching and transforming sentient beings will not be in vain;
If one’s practice of teaching and transforming beings is not in vain, Then one will attain wisdom and eloquence without limit.
If one attains wisdom and eloquence that are boundless, One may expound this inconceivable Dharma;
If one attains the inconceivable power of preaching the Dharma, One causes immeasurable multitudes to rejoice.
If one attains the joy and celebration of immeasurable multitudes, And accumulates inconceivable eons of practice,
If one attains such vast and great conduct, Each and every one will be able to know it through their power of wisdom.
If one attains such power of wisdom, one transforms sentient beings in the world according to their types;
once one has transformed sentient beings according to their needs, they all attain the knowledge of abiding in past lives.
If one attains such knowledge of past lives, the three karmas will be pure and constant without interruption;
if the three karmas are constant without interruption, one will arrive wherever one thinks of by the power of one's own vows.

If one attains the power of aspiration, one reaches wherever mindfulness turns; manifesting in various forms according to all sentient beings, if one can thus manifest in accordance with the types of beings, one will attain inconceivable and wondrous sounds.
If one attains such wondrous sounds and voices, capable of producing all manner of speech,
and if the exquisite words thus uttered can pervade all worlds.
Thus pervading all worlds, they are able to know them all within a single kṣaṇa;
having thus attained such understanding of the minds of all beings, they are neither born nor extinguished, and never regress.
If one is free from arising and ceasing, there is no regression; all obstacles and afflictions will no longer arise.
Once obstacles and afflictions no longer arise, the merits, wisdom, and the Dharma-body become perfected.
If one attains the wisdom of the Dharma-body, its radiant light of Dharma-practice illuminates the world;
if one attains the light of the Dharma that illuminates the world, then one attains the ten stages and the ten kinds of bodies.
If one attains the ten kinds of bodies of the tenth stage, then one attains the path of liberation through prajñā;
if one attains the path of liberation through prajñā, then the consecration and adornment become supreme.
Once one has received such an empowerment, the path of samādhi is entirely perfected;
having attained such samādhi, one beholds all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Having seen these Buddhas in this manner, and having reflected upon this matter while those Buddhas contemplate conferring the empowerment,
the Buddhas of the ten directions collectively confer the empowerment.
When all Buddhas simultaneously confer empowerment, each extends his right hand to stroke their crowns;
having received the stroking of the crowns by all Buddhas, they are then able to manifest transformations as vast as space.
Thus manifested, equal to space, it remains steadfast wherever it abides;
if one attains such steadfastness, neither gods nor humans can fathom it.
Since neither humans nor devas can fathom it, such deeds transcend all measurement;
surpassing all measures and beyond the reach of language—this is the power of the non-void of all things.
By this power of the non-emptiness of all things, one who hears the name or beholds the body shall obtain great eloquence;
since such is the power of great eloquence, one is able to act as a great benefactor to the world.
He is further named the "Non-empty Great Being," for he abides as a being of his original nature;
never abandoning great compassion, he proclaims the wondrous Dharma and transforms sentient beings within all the evil realms.
He proclaims the supreme vehicle of Jewel Light, like a mass of vajra-jewel clouds;
its intrinsic nature is like a jewel from the ocean—neither increasing nor decreasing, it is without diminution.
Boundless merit is likewise so: in lands where there is no Buddha and the Dharma is not heard, he manifests there as a Buddha’s Bodhi;
seeing him is like beholding a great treasury of the Dharma.
He constantly preaches the Dharma, free from all delusions; throughout the worlds of the ten directions, he is without obstruction.
Like the light of the moon shining everywhere, he teaches and transforms sentient beings through a thousand skillful means.
In every single moment of the Buddha’s bodhi, one directly perceives all worlds in the ten directions;
constantly turning the wheel of Dharma to bring peace to the world, they valiantly and universally turn it throughout the realms of the ten directions.
Those stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, adorned with the infinite transformations of the Buddha,
he traverses again for inconceivable eons, personally approaching to transform all sentient beings.
Whether male or female, boy or girl, among the classes of devas, humans, asuras, and nāga kings,
down to yakṣas and mahoragas— all are seen through the wisdom of liberation.
Whatever various forms exist in all the worlds, And whatever languages they may employ, The Valiant One perceives them all completely; Thus does the Valiant One observe them all.
The Ocean-Seal Samādhi is born from the mouth; having attained this Ocean-Seal and its manifold samādhis, one can adorn inconceivable lands.
One makes offerings to all Tathāgatas of the ten directions; having thus performed these various kinds of offerings,
Furthermore, one attains the array of radiant ornaments;
then one attains the wisdom of boundless liberation. If one attains the wisdom of boundless liberation, one achieves inconceivable transformations of the body.
The eloquence of speech and the eloquence of wisdom are likewise; if one attains unimpeded eloquence of speech and wisdom, their giving and transformations are inconceivable.
It is the same for morality, patience, and diligence; if one attains mastery in morality, patience, and diligence, [the results are likewise inconceivable].
The spiritual transformations of meditative concentration are unfathomable.
He gives rise to the wisdom of skillful means and spiritual transformations; having attained this wisdom of skillful means and spiritual transformations, he brings forth boundless merits.
Through samādhi, one enters a single atom, and all atoms are entirely entered;
within a single atom are inconceivable lands, and within every single atom, all are seen.
Thus, within as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms, all those Buddha-fields are beheld;
various subtle and pure assemblies, supreme, precious, and wondrous lands,
arise in the world according to reality, with their secret and sublime ascensions therein.
Some dispel darkness and emit radiant light, With Indra-nets layer upon layer, inexhaustible.
Just as one perceives a single great radiance, So too do all such atoms reach their end.
This Great Sage’s practice of samādhi Is itself the boundless, supreme liberation.
With the power of samādhi, they make offerings to the Buddhas;
having made offerings to all Tathāgatas, they further transform thousands of millions of things from their hands, acting as great beings to present vast offerings.
Even unto the exquisite flower garlands and the wafting, rarest incenses of the ten directions,
he personally offered each one from his own hand as he approached the Buddha beneath the Great Bodhi Tree.
Wondrous garments of incalculable value, various banners, streamers, and parasols,
and ornaments of Jāmbūnada gold— these he personally bestowed with his own hands.
All infinite objects of enjoyment, Purely offered to the Great Sage,
Presented with hands in total renunciation, Abiding at the foot of the King of Trees, the Bodhi of the Buddha.
Even unto all the various musical troupes, striking drums to produce manifold wondrous sounds,
with diverse elegant instruments such as lutes and harps, each one personally struck and played by their hands.
With various hymns and sublime verses, and diverse praises of his true virtues,
he performs them all from within his own hands throughout the infinite realms of the ten directions.
Some perform buddha-works by means of light, all of which move in a clockwise direction;
they sprinkle fragrant water throughout all buddha-fields as an offering to the Lamps of the World.
Radiant, magnificent, and pleasing fragrances, Inconceivable lotus-garlands,
And countless wondrously colored lotuses— Each one spontaneously created as offerings to all Buddhas.
Emitting great light and adorned with flowers, a vast ocean of clouds of various subtle and wondrous blossoms;
such marvelous flowers pervade everywhere, performing the work of a Buddha through this expansive offering.
Emitting great light adorned with fragrance, A vast ocean of clouds of various subtle perfumes,
Such wondrous scents pervade everywhere, Performing the work of Buddhas through this vast offering.

Emitting great light, they offer ointment incense; A wondrous ocean-cloud of various kinds of ointment incense, Such ointment incense pervades everywhere, Performing the Buddha-work of vast offerings.
Emitting great garlands of radiant light as adornments, clouds and oceans of various subtle and exquisite garlands pervade everywhere;
through these wondrous garlands, they perform vast offerings as acts of Buddha-work.
They emit great radiance and clouds of powdered incense, a wondrous ocean of various kinds of powdered incense;
such sublime fragrances pervade everywhere, performing the work of Buddhas through vast offerings.
Emitting great radiance, they manifest clouds of oceans of various subtle and wondrous robes;
such exquisite garments pervade everywhere, performing the work of Buddhas through vast offerings.
Emitting great light, they manifest canopies of exquisite adornment;
Cloud-seas of various subtle and wondrous canopies, Such marvelous canopies pervade everywhere, Performing the work of Buddhas through vast offerings.
Emitting great light adorned with jewels, Various subtle and wondrous clouds of jewels like an ocean;
Such wondrous jewels pervading everywhere, Performing vast offerings as a Buddha-activity.
Emitting great light adorned with lotuses, A wondrous ocean-clouds of various lotus flowers;
Such exquisite blossoms pervade everywhere, Performing the Buddha-work through vast offerings.
They emit great light adorned with necklaces, oceans of clouds of various exquisite necklaces;
such necklaces pervade everywhere, performing the Buddha-work of vast offerings.
He emits the magnificent adornment of the great banner of light;
that banner is blue, yellow, red, and white, adorned with countless exquisite jewels, and these various banners beautify that Buddha-field.
Various kinds of adorned mani-jewel nets, with suspended silken banners, canopies, and exquisite flower garlands;
hanging pearl necklaces that proclaim the Buddha’s voice, they hold up parasols ever above the Tathāgata.
Even if one were to make offerings to a single Tathāgata, personally providing for them in incalculable numbers,
and were to do so for all Buddhas without exception— this is the *ṛṣi-vikurvaṇa-samādhi*.
The supernormal knowledge that encompasses all worlds is the supreme samādhi;
by skillfully employing all manner of expedient means, one thus transforms and guides all sentient beings.
Some make offerings to the Tathāgatas, performing inconceivable acts of giving in various ways;
their ethical discipline is pure, they practice the dhūta austerities, and their patience is inexhaustible and unshakable.
Some possess courageous and diligent vigor, Tranquilly practicing and cultivating meditative concentration;
With wisdom they thoroughly comprehend all meanings and principles, And are able to employ every skillful means for goodness.
Whether practicing the vows of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, or equanimity; through the power of shared purpose, kind speech, and benefiting others;
by accumulating all meritorious deeds with wisdom; one attains liberation through the Four Truths and the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination.
Some practice the faculties, powers, and factors of enlightenment to attain liberation through the Śrāvaka vehicle;
they contemplate dependent origination for the pure Pratyekabuddha vehicle; and through supernatural powers and transformations, they follow the Supreme Vehicle.
Whether one perceives impermanence and various sufferings, or the sudden and violent masses that are neither life nor body,
nor the entanglements of untimely afflictions and obstacles— the power of samādhi can eliminate them all.
Practicing diligence throughout all worlds, He expounds the wondrous Dharma to transform all beings;
May all universally attain liberation, Guiding sentient beings according to the world.
Those various forms and types are impossible to fathom; They secretly manifest samādhis through their supernormal powers.

Adorned with the mastery of desire and delight in wondrous transformations, They guide all worlds according to their inclinations, Causing everyone to rejoice and attain peace and happiness, Never for a moment ceasing to keep sentient beings in mind.
If one encounters times of famine and manifold hardships, may all the various comforts and joys found in the world,
and all that is beloved, arise from their hearts and be extensively provided for all the world.
Constantly with foods and drinks of rare flavor, With various beautiful garments and treasuries—
The royal possessions I cherish and delight in giving away, I bestow them upon all the world according to their wishes.
His body is adorned with extraordinary and wondrous marks; Majestic and sublime, his conduct is unshakable.
With ointments, incense, and flower garlands, he delights the hearts of all; Manifesting these physical forms, he transforms all living beings.

Those who see him feel love and give rise to joy; with various colors of supreme and wondrous wisdom, he beholds all most sublime and subtle forms, transforming and guiding the world according to their inclinations.
The kalaviṅka utters wondrous sounds; The white goose and the kinnara produce voices like the *kinnara’s drum*, Constantly expounding the Tathāgata’s Dharma of liberation.
The eighty-four thousand Tathāgatagarbhas— able to practice all supreme truths and skillfully proclaim the distinctions of the myriad dharmas—
they transform and guide all sentient beings according to their inclinations.
He undergoes all the sufferings and afflictions of sentient beings; it is likewise with that which is neither evil nor good.
Performing all manner of karmic actions, he transforms and guides all sentient beings according to their inclinations.
If one encounters the suffering of calamities and afflictions, seeing such unbearable hardships,
may they take upon themselves all the sufferings of sentient beings, bringing peace and happiness to all the worlds.
Whether phenomena exist or do not arise, for those lacking wisdom, merit, and liberation, you explain them thoroughly alongside the King;
thus you deliver sentient beings and enable them to transcend to the other shore.
Able to leave behind the bonds of craving and all fetters, He is named the Lord of Liberation in the World;
Having transcended all sensual pleasures, He shines with the light of renunciation and liberation.
He emits ten kinds of radiant light and is able to practice the various skillful means for taming and guiding beings;
he fully understands all the practices of the sages and observes the world according to its activities.
Sentient beings are equal to Amitāyus, Serene, secure, and joyful;
Birth, old age, and the suffering of illness cannot invade them, And they will certainly perceive for themselves the realm beyond impermanence.
Just as there are sentient beings who delight in the light of lamps, [he] kindles a great torch for the darkness of worldly ignorance;
though the sufferings of old age, sickness, and death constantly blaze, he guides all sentient beings in the world.
The ten powers, diligence, and the four fearlessnesses, The eighteen unique qualities of a Tathāgata—
I contemplate these vast merits in my mind, Performing the work of a Buddha throughout all worlds.
Just as various worldly illusions can manifest all manner of forms and appearances, so too are the emanations of the Tathāgatas seen;
through such spiritual transformations, they guide all beings in existence.
Through various skillful means and practices, he entices and instructs all sentient beings with virtuous words;
like a lotus flower unsullied by water, he performs diverse deeds according to his will.
With flowery speech and swift eloquence in all languages, they engage in singing, dancing, play, and mutual grappling;
adorned with necklaces, they dance and whirl, manifesting various illusory forms, each distinct from the others.
Sometimes he appears as a village headman, a merchant lord, an elder, a caravan leader, or a master of the marketplace;
as a counselor, a great minister, or a royal attendant; or as a physician, a man of great eloquence, or a master of many treatises.
In the wilderness, you become a great tree, an inexhaustible treasury of precious jewels and wondrous medicines;
as a wish-fulfilling mani-gem, you provide all that is needed, and for those who have lost their way or are bewildered, you act as a guide.

He fully knows all future births within the world; yet sentient beings do not know that they themselves create their karma, engaging instead in various skillful means such as farming and labor, or in the diverse practices of worldly arts and crafts.
Sometimes manifesting as enemy or kin without hatred or love, bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings;
thoroughly illuminating the various teachings of the treatises, that Sage opens and clarifies the path of radiant light.
If one practices the supreme conduct of the Great Sage, one attains liberation in both the heavens and the human realm;
for those who have gone forth and practice asceticism, it opens the way to that supreme, all-encompassing wisdom.
If there are those among the various non-Buddhist renunciants who constantly maintain silence, O Gautama,
who bear the marks of naked ascetics and motionless yogis, and who likewise rely upon and follow the teachings of their own original teachers.
Some constantly maintain the dharma of self-sacrifice; some cling to the notion that there is a self or that it is originally non-existent.
With long hair tied in topknots like youthful boys, they likewise rely upon and follow their own original teachers.

Some, on certain days, roast their bodies five times; observing the dog-vow or the ox-vow, wearing deerskin garments, they travel to pay homage at the three periods of the day, likewise relying upon and following their own teachers.
Some constantly delight in celestial wisdom, denying both good and evil while repudiating causes;
seeking roots and fruits as their food, they cling to them as a supreme, inconceivable flavor.
Some squat while wearing red robes; some smear themselves with ashes or lie upon grass;
some carry staffs inscribed with their names draped over their shoulders, each likewise following the instructions of their own teacher.
Even down to each and every non-Buddhist practitioner, he causes them all to be free from their fetters;
though they practice harmful wisdom and cruel austerities, he guides and draws in all such non-Buddhists.

He transforms all those of similar kind in the world; To those who dwell in false views at his sacred sites, He skillfully expounds the wondrous Dharma, Proclaiming this True Teaching so that others may practice it.
Some expound the true mantra practices of the Mahāyāna, the sublime words of the essential secrets of the True Dharma;
some expound truthful speech with straightforwardness, while among them, some expound the wondrous verses of the devas;
some attain liberation through written characters—the wondrous meanings of the Dharma-assembly and the adamantine phrases.
With wisdom he destroys the phrases of external treatises, And expounds various words concerning liberation.
He may proclaim divine mantras among human beings, Proclaiming all manner of wondrous verses;
Among these there may be the language of devas, The language of nāga kings, or the phrases of yakṣas.
Whether among rākṣasas, bhūtas, yakṣas, piśācas, gandharvas,
kinnara maidens, or garuḍas, they proclaim this sublime Dharma, the meaning of liberation.
He speaks according to the Dharma with wisdom; whether it be the Buddha or the Dharma, all such things are exhausted therein.
This path of wisdom is an inconceivable dharma, wherein he explains this transformation of samādhi.
Having realized the samādhi of the world, they move through all worlds;
sometimes they emit inconceivable light, and that light draws in and guides all sentient beings.
Or he emits a light named "Sublime Contemplation," such that when sentient beings gain faith through this light,
they attain non-empty sublime observation, supreme wisdom, and its supreme cause.
One attains the sight of all Buddhas and hears their Dharma, As well as witnessing the manifold virtues of the Saṅgha;
Beholding the stupas and praising the Buddha is most rare, And one beholds the illumination of pure radiance.
Some emit a light named "Universal Illumination," Which shines throughout all worlds;
He knows every single atom within them, And speaks for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to the world.
That light shines universally upon all sentient beings; They constantly hold lamps as offerings to the Buddhas.
Having offered lamps to all the Buddhas, [They become] all the lamps and lights in the world.
Whether with lamps of ghee or oil, Or lamps of pine resin, grass, bamboo, or reeds,
With lamps of various fragrances, exquisite flavors, or precious jewels— They offer all these radiant lights to the Buddhas.

Again, he emits a light named "Universal Illumination," Which is able to observe all sentient beings Sunk in the ocean of birth and death through craving and attachment, In order to rescue and deliver all living beings.
May your light illuminate the ocean of craving within saṃsāra, Bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings;
May they all be freed from the four māras, And, released from the oppression of suffering, find peace and joy.
He constructed countless bridges, or provided boats and rafts upon rivers and roads;
he rebuked the false and praised those who bring peace; emitting light, he illuminated them all.
With light that awakens those who are parched with thirst, he is able to enlighten all sentient beings;
having distanced himself from desire and attained sublime benefit, he becomes a guide who expounds the Dharma.
If one attains wholesome benefit by departing from sensual desire, so too does one teach the Dharma to transform and guide others;
having attained Buddhahood and showered down the water of ambrosia, one rescues and delivers those in the world who suffer from hunger and thirst.
Some construct ponds, rivers, wells, and reservoirs; they dig and build for the sake of awakening.
They revile sensual desire and praise meditative concentration; they condemn craving and attachment, and thus eliminate them all.
Out of compassion for sentient beings, he emits radiant light; that light universally awakens all living beings.
Delighting in the transformations for others and abiding in Bodhi, may I give rise to this mind in every thought-moment.
Adorned with the marks and signs upon a lotus seat, With great compassion, he takes pity on all sentient beings;
He constantly proclaims the virtues of the Buddha, Emitting light that causes them to rejoice.
Again, he emits a light named "Pleasing," which can awaken all sentient beings so that they conceive love and respect for the Buddha and the Dharma, and take delight in constantly serving the Saṃgha.
Having attained the Buddha-dharma, they give rise to joy and celebration;
by serving the assembly of monks and paying homage to the sublime merits of the Tathāgata, they thereby attain the unsurpassed practice of the Buddhas.
Having encountered all the Tathāgatas and the sublime Dharma, I have attained the most unsurpassed practice of patience;
Awakening these many sentient beings, I mindfully recollect the Buddha, the Dharma, and the holy virtues.
Each and every merit is awakened by the mind; it emits radiance to inspire seekers, and again emits radiance to gather merit—this light can awaken all sentient beings.
Having practiced countless varieties of giving, they entreated others toward unsurpassed great enlightenment;
whatever they sought was fulfilled according to their wishes, for they were able to bestow such diverse things.
Having established everything according to one's will, they accumulate merit and radiate light;
thus do the wise radiate light, and that light illuminates and observes all sentient beings.
The single Dharma proclaimed from the mouth is inexhaustible; in a single kṣaṇa, one can eloquently expound and discern it.
The wisdom of the Dharma encompasses the meaning for all sentient beings, and through the wisdom of wisdom, one is able to know it all completely.
The supreme meaning of the wondrous Dharma has been proclaimed; wisdom itself emits that great radiance.
If one uses the lamp of wisdom to emit light, that light will illuminate and examine all sentient beings.
Sentient beings are not empty and are without arising or ceasing; The self-nature of all phenomena is itself without nature.
They are like illusions, like mists, and like the moon reflected in water; They are like dreams and also like images in a mirror.
The Dharma has no sovereign and relies upon emptiness; it skillfully explains the arising of the lamp of wisdom.
Through the transformative power of the Dharma, it radiates light, and that light awakens all sentient beings.
Who can easily attain the inexhaustible dhāraṇī, which upholds the wondrous Dharma-treasury of all Tathāgatas?
Having cultivated this dhāraṇī of the wondrous Dharma, one shall constantly protect and uphold the Dharma of the Great Sage.
Proclaiming and expounding this Dharma for the sake of the world—this is the radiance of the transformation of the Dharma;
or, by means of excellent relinquishment, one emits radiance, and that light can awaken all sentient beings.
Knowing that impermanence does not endure, one attains happiness by thus relinquishing it all;
even if sentient beings are difficult for me to subdue, I understand their nature to be like floating clouds.
Having understood this, with excellent wisdom and peaceful harmony, one shines forth the light of noble generosity.
Again, he emits a light named "Repentance," Which illuminates and examines all sentient beings who have violated the prohibitions;
Once they have repented and purified their precepts, Their minds give rise to the aspiration that they shall attain Buddhahood.
If there are sentient beings who, by virtue of upholding the precepts, purify their present karma of breaking those prohibitions,
and they likewise give rise to this bodhicitta— this light is emitted so that they may all fully repent.
The light of patience emits a multitude of adornments; that light shines upon and examines all sentient beings.
For those whose minds of anger are extremely evil and difficult to tame, patience first removes them.
Personally undertaking the difficult practice of patience, remaining unshakable in the mind upon the path to enlightenment,
and constantly praising the practice of patience— this constitutes the manifold adornment of patience.
Again, he emits radiant beams of light, Shining upon and examining all indolent sentient beings;
Through the supreme and wondrous skillful means of the Triple Gem, They offer worship continuously for a long time.
Having continuously made offerings through the various skillful means of the Three Jewels,
one is then able to remain far removed from the four māras and swiftly attain the unsurpassed, great bodhi.

Transforming all sentient beings through the practice of diligence, and having thus made offerings to the Triple Gem, one constantly upholds the wondrous Dharma without end; such a person shall attain radiant brilliance.
Again, he emits light that practices patience, universally observing all sentient beings;
through awakening, he remains far removed from greed, hatred, and delusion, attaining a mind that is constant and uninterrupted at all times.
All karmic actions are entirely eliminated, And all that is unwholesome is distanced.
Praising the pacification of calamities and extolling meditative concentration, With pure patience, they radiate brilliant light.
Adorned with wisdom, they radiate light, Able to awaken all sentient beings from the darkness of delusion;
If they preach the True Dharma, liberation is attained, And they are able to universally realize and enter all roots of wisdom.
If one hears the true Dharma and attains liberation, Having been able to reach the very source everywhere,
One immediately attains the *sūryapradīpa* samādhi, And obtains the wondrous radiance of the Buddha’s wisdom.
Whatever the King possesses, I am able to give away, seeking the sublime Dharma and abiding in Bodhi;
thus I shall always expound this Dharma, attaining the adornment of the light of wisdom.
When the Buddha emits this great radiance, that light illuminates and examines all sentient beings;
countless, inconceivable thousands of Tathāgatas appear seated upon exquisite lotus flowers.
The Greatly Awakened Tathāgata liberates me; With boundless transformations, he proclaims the Buddha’s voice.
Acting as the power of all Tathāgatas’ illumination and inspection, He immediately emits this Buddha-light.
Again, he emits a light that bestows fearlessness; for those beings who are terrified by spirits (*bhūta*) and afflicted by calamities,
fetters, and bonds— those who suffer such terrors and disasters—
he causes all sentient beings to attain peace and security, so that they may all be able to remain far removed from taking life.
Rescuing those afflicted by the perils of the paths of karma, they attain great fearlessness and radiate light.
Again, they emit a light named "Peaceful Bliss," which settles those entangled in chronic illness;
it completely cures all epidemics and brings about the peace of dhyāna and samādhi.
Various medicines, flowers, fruits, and seeds; Scented unguents, powdered incense, precious gems, and flavors;
Fragrant waters, milk, honey, and clarified butter; All offerings of food and drink are fully provided.
Seeing all Tathāgatas emitting radiant light, They illuminate and observe sentient beings at the time of death;
Teaching them to practice mindfulness of the Buddha so that they may see the Buddha, They ensure that at the end of life, these beings will certainly be reborn in a Buddha-field.
If one recollects the Buddha at the time of death, And beholds the Buddha’s image with love and reverence,
The Buddha will go there to deliver them, Enabling them to see all Buddhas as they preach the Dharma.
Again, he emits a light named "Dharma-light," which can awaken all sentient beings;
by hearing the Dharma, copying it, reading and reciting it, and upholding it, they shall always find joy and delight in all dharmas.
The blossoming of the sublime Dharma is extremely difficult to encounter; Diligently seeking the sublime Dharma fulfills one's heart's desire.
By means of various skillful expedients, this Dharma is attained; Therefore, the light of the teaching of the Dharma is obtained.
Again, they emit a light named "Language," by which the sons of the Buddha awaken those sentient beings;
the sound of their original vows vibrates through the trichiliocosm, so that all hear the various voices and sounds of the Tathāgatas.

Having praised the Great Sage with a loud voice, and having offered bells and chimes with a resonant sound, one becomes the Buddha’s speech for all the world; therefore, one attains this light of speech.
Again, he emits a light that bestows ambrosia; that light can awaken all sentient beings.
When it perceives the moment a being gives rise to a thought, it brings about practice in accord with all meritorious virtues.
Amidst countless afflictions and calamities, They constantly speak of falsehoods and find no peace;
If one can always bring these to rest and eliminate them, It is said that by bestowing the nectar of immortality, all shall attain it.
Again, he emits a light named "Most Supreme"; this light can awaken all sentient beings, as do supreme morality and samādhi, enabling them to hear of the Buddha’s most supreme great wisdom.
With peerless, pure ethical discipline and samādhi, the Great Sage, supreme in wisdom, extols and praises the giving of bodhicitta; such a person shall attain this sublime radiance.
To bestow inexhaustible and wondrous jewels, these treasures were offered to the Great Sage;

by giving such treasures as offerings to the Buddha and his stūpas, sentient beings who seek jewels yet do not obtain them shall attain Buddhahood through the gift of all precious gems. Therefore, he emits light adorned like jewels.
Again, they emit light that shines forth afar; this light awakens all sentient beings.
Though people may not smell pleasant ointments or incense, they practice the meritorious conduct of the Tathāgata.
The incense produced in the heavens and among humans, used as an offering to all Tathāgatas,
and with which I have entirely anointed many Buddha-stūpas— for this reason, I emit this light of ointment-incense.
The Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī-ratna-prabhāsa Sūtra, Scroll Four;
The Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī-ratna-prabhāsa Sūtra, Scroll Five.
[Translated at] Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India, in the Land of the West.
The Tripitaka Master Dengyō, the Śramaṇa of Imperial Purple Robes, the Subject Hōten, says:
“Furthermore, they emit light of various adornments, Various banners, pennants, and parasols;
They produce all manner of music and manifold incenses, And hold fast to exquisite flowers and fragrances.”
Thus they made various offerings to the Buddha: flowers, incense, and powdered incense;
banners, pennants, and exquisite canopies draped with jeweled curtains, producing all manner of wondrous adornments.
Again, emitting light that inspires pure minds, they stand holding various jewels at the site of the stūpa of the Pure Great Sage Buddha, attaining this pure and wondrous radiance.
Again, they emit vast clouds of radiant light, And rain down various kinds of exquisite unguents;
Sprinkling scented water upon the ground of the stupa precincts, They therefore obtain these clouds of radiance.
Again, he emits light of various adornments, so that those who are naked obtain clothing for their decoration;
with various necklaces and various garments, he thus brings forth the gift of adornment.
Again, he emits a light named "Various Flavors," Bestowing supreme flavors upon those who suffer from hunger and thirst;
Having bestowed various kinds of superior food and drink, He attains a great radiance.

Again, he emits a light named "Ultimate Meaning," which bestows treasures from storehouses upon the poor and offers them to the Triple Gem without end; thus, the practice of giving is perfected in its ultimate meaning.
Furthermore, he emits a light called "Pure Eyes," by which the blind perceive all forms and appearances;
by offering lamps to the Buddha and the Buddha-stūpas, one obtains this light-emitting, pure eye.
Again, he emits a light called "Purity of the Ear," by which those who are deaf each come to hear all manner of sounds;
having offered music to the Buddha and to the Buddha-stūpas, they obtain this pure, radiant ear.
Furthermore, he emits a light called "Pure Nose": those with impaired olfactory faculties who have offered exquisite fragrant ointments to the Buddha and his stūpas obtain a nose of pure radiance.
Again, they emit the light of the pure tongue, Attaining the Buddha’s soft and compassionate speech;
Far removed from coarse, harsh, and impure words, They obtain the auspicious mark of the radiant tongue.
Again, he emits a light called "Purity of Body": those with incomplete physical faculties become complete;
they relinquish their bodies to be equal in measure to the Buddhas and their stūpas—thereby they attain this pure body.
Again, they emit a light called "Pure Intention," through which all sublime intentions are attained;
by means of the mind and thought, they practice samādhi, thereby obtaining this light of pure intention.
Again, he emits a light of pure color; Those who contemplate wish to see the various physical marks of the Benevolent King.
All manner of wondrous colors pervade everywhere, Attaining the majestic adornment of the Tower of Radiance.
Again, he emits a light of pure sound; He fully knows all sounds that are non-sound and empty sounds.
Faith arises just like an echo in a valley; Thus he emits this light of pure sound.
Again, he emits the light of pure fragrance, Turning all foul odors into exquisite perfumes;
Sprinkling sublime fragrant water upon the Buddha’s stūpas and temples, He emits this light and abides here at the Bodhi tree.

Again, he emits the light of pure flavor, Which transforms the poisonous and non-poisonous into supreme tastes, Offering them to the Buddha, the śrāvakas, and one’s parents; By bestowing these supreme flavors, one attains this light.
Again, he emits a light that touches with purity; rough, slippery, and soft sensations all become blissful.
Swords, spears, arrows, and lances, like clouds and rain, are transformed into supple and exquisite flower garlands.
Countless beings obtain peace through the touch of soft garments as they cross over to the presence of the Buddha.
Exquisite flowers, fragrant ointments, and pure robes; One attains the giving of garlands and canopies that radiate light.
Furthermore, one emits the pure light of the Dharma; All inconceivable dharmas within a single hair-tip appear for the sake of all worlds, And one attains the Buddha’s exposition of all dharmas.
Believing that the self-nature of phenomena is fundamentally unarisen, And that the Dharma-body and Reward-body are likewise so;
That phenomena eternally abide in quiescence, equal to space— For this reason, one attains the pure Dharma.

The manifestation of light should be performed; from a single hair-tip on the face of the Great Sage, rays of light as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are produced, each according to its respective karmic cause.
Just as from a single hair-tip or speck of dust in the present moment, there appear as many forms as the atoms of the Ganges River;
when all such hairs have been exhausted, this Great Sage manifests through samādhi.
If he emits radiance according to his original practice, the deeds performed by this light are identical to those of the past;
if he did not manifest this radiance, how could his spiritual transformations equal those of the Great Sage?
Since the merit obtained by him is the same as the cause, so too are rejoicing and entreaty;
if anyone should behold it, all shall obtain peace, for this light brings understanding to both self and others.

If one performs meritorious deeds with peaceful harmony, Continuing them without interruption to make offerings to the Buddha, One should joyfully seek the virtues of the Tathāgata; Beholding this radiance, act in this manner.
Just as a blind person does not behold the sun, And cannot distinguish day from night or the world,
How could the eyes and other faculties perceive forms, Or understand the specific meanings of their respective phenomena?
The Tamer likewise emits rays of light, clearly manifesting them to others while remaining unseen himself;
yet for those who have not abandoned inverted delusive thoughts, they shall ultimately fail to attain the profoundly penetrating mind.

Riding upon a precious palace adorned with every ornament, and equipped with various necessities, exquisite incense, and flowers—none among the great assembly can know it; his illness is exceedingly difficult to dispel.
The light of the Tamer is likewise: this light itself obscures him so that he cannot be known.
Deceitful and false speech has not yet been eliminated, and the mind ultimately lacks vastness;
yet, by discerning this radiance, one constantly attains eloquence and peace.
His body is free from doubt and devoid of false conceptualization; detached from self, he is a great banner of merit.
Adorned with transformations of principal and attendant figures, he relies upon this unsurpassed samādhi.
Throughout the infinite ten directions, he reveals the sons of the Buddha along with their primary and attendant retinues;
within various worlds as numerous as the motes of dust in a trichiliocosm, light ornaments lotus thrones.
All bodies sit together in the full lotus posture, manifesting this samādhi through transformation;
in worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten buddha-fields, they and their retinues sit upon lotus flowers.

Each surrounded by a host of Buddha-sons, Abiding in the samādhi of universal entry, They employ the power of transformation and guidance of the Great Sages; Sentient beings emerge from the merit of the Buddhas.
They mutually surround the great lotus, simultaneously joining their palms in reverent homage;
this Dharma is that of the Great Tamer, who has entered the samādhi of tranquility.
Surrounded by a multitude of disciples, like the bright moon amidst the stars,
he enters into every direction, manifesting the sons of the Buddha and their retinues.
Throughout all directions these are entirely exhausted; this samādhi manifests through transformations.
Those directions that were covered and closed are all cleared away, as one enters the practice of the supreme samādhi.
Some arise from samādhi, manifesting their own bodies throughout the ten directions;
some, while in samādhi in the east, can cause vibration without rising in the west;
some, while in samādhi in the west, manifest the marks of a Great Man in the east.
They are able to enter all these ten directions, And further manifest various samādhis in different lands.
They can extensively manifest this wisdom of merit, The great seer’s supernormal transformations and samādhi;
If one were to exhaust all lands in every direction, Countless Tathāgatas would all go there.
He pays homage at the soles of each foot, dwelling now in the Samādhi of Peaceful Bliss;
or, through this samādhi, he gazes upon sentient beings, until the lands of the western quarter are all serene and still.
All Tathāgatas appear before me, manifesting countless offerings;
having thus seen them all the way to the western quarter, I proceed again to incalculable Buddha-fields,
where I pay homage at their feet and attain the samādhi of dwelling in peace and bliss.
Through meditative concentration he perceives correctly; throughout all the lands of the eastern direction, all Tathāgatas appear before him, and he beholds countless offerings as well.
Having entered these Buddha-fields of the ten directions, remaining entirely unmoved in each and every one,
they manifest various samādhis therein and present manifold offerings to the Lamps of the World.
Within the samādhi of the eye-object, he is able to manifest great forms and various realms;
seeing these inconceivable forms, all in the heavens and among humans are struck with wonder.
Having already beheld the samādhi of the sensory object of form, one reflects thus upon the objective sphere of the eye:
"The intrinsic nature of the eye is neither arising nor ceasing; therefore, I shall reveal signlessness and emptiness."
In the samādhi of the "Dust of the Ear," one can manifest the realms of great sounds;
entering into all languages and voices, both heavens and humans are utterly amazed.
Having already beheld the samādhi of the auditory object, one thoroughly contemplates the sphere of the ear-object;
the self-nature of the ear is neither arising nor ceasing, and thus one reveals the signless emptiness.
In the Samādhi of Nasal Dust, one can manifest great fragrant realms;
such wondrous scents pervade everywhere, leaving both gods and humans utterly amazed.
Having already beheld the samādhi of the olfactory object, he further contemplates the sphere of the nasal object with clear attention:
the self-nature of the nose is neither arising nor ceasing; therefore, he expounds the signless emptiness.
In the samādhi of the gustatory dust, one can manifest the realm of the great gustatory dust;
such supreme flavors pervade everywhere, leaving both gods and humans utterly amazed.
Having already attained the Samādhi of Supreme Flavor, one minutely contemplates the sensory realm of the tongue;
the self-nature of the tongue is neither arising nor ceasing, and thus one reveals the signless emptiness.
Within the samādhi of the tactile object of the body, he is able to manifest the realm of great tangible objects;
as these worldly tactile objects pervade everywhere, all beings in the heavens and among humans are utterly amazed.
Having already beheld the samādhi of the sense-object of touch, one thoroughly contemplates the pervasive arising of the sense-object of the body;
since the intrinsic nature of the body is neither born nor extinguished, one thereby elucidates signless emptiness.
Or, within the samādhi of mental objects, one can manifest the realm of great dharmic objects;
having already beheld the samādhi of dharmic objects, one then contemplates the realm of mental objects with careful attention.
Since the intrinsic nature of the mind is neither arising nor ceasing, one thereby elucidates signless emptiness.
By means of the samādhi of an infant body, he manifests and dwells in the full bloom of youth;
having manifested the samādhi of youth, he again dwells in a body decrepit with old age and chronic infirmity.
Abiding in this samādhi of an aged body, he further resolves his mind to become a lay devotee (upāsaka).
Abiding in this Upāsaka-samādhi, one transforms one’s nature and manifests as the body of a bhikṣu;
abiding in this Bhikṣu-body-samādhi, one immediately attains the body of a bhikṣu of great learning.
Abiding in this samādhi of the body of much learning, one immediately attains the bodies of those in training and those beyond training;
having already abided in such a samādhi of the body, one then abides in the body of the Tathāgata.
Abiding in this Tathāgata-body samādhi, one attains the Buddha’s most supreme and wondrous form-body;
abiding in this supreme body-samādhi, the transformation-body manifests in the forms of devas and humans.
From this samādhi of the celestial form-body, there arise the bodies of many great nāgas;
from this samādhi of the great nāga-body, there arise the bodies of all the great yakṣas.
From this yakṣa-body samādhi, all bhūta-bodies are produced;
from this bhūta-body samādhi, a single hair-tip manifests before one.
From this samādhi of a single hair-tip, all hair-tips are produced;
from within all these hair-tips, a single particle of a hair-tip is produced.
From this samādhi of a single hair-tip mote, all hair-tip motes appear;
within each and every samādhi of a hair-tip mote, one can further manifest as many [samādhis] as there are motes of dust.
Having seen the samādhi of a single atom, one gives rise to all atoms without exception;
having seen the samādhi of each and every atom, one gives rise to the adamantine limit of the great ocean.
From this Vajra-limit samādhi, the flowers and fruits of the maṇi tree emerge;
from this maṇi-tree samādhi, the great radiance of the Tathāgata appears.
From this Tathāgata-light samādhi, all the waters of rivers and seas emerge;
from within this river-and-sea samādhi, the realm of great masses of fire once again appears.
From this fire-dust samādhi, the thought of wind-dust arises;
from this wind-dust samādhi, the realm of earth-dust arises.
From this Samādhi of the Dust of the Ground, all celestial palaces are produced;
within this Samādhi of the Palaces, one contemplates them as equal to the realm of empty space.
With inconceivable samādhis and liberations, they have fully attained boundless merits;
they can further illuminate infinite eons, for all Tathāgatas are utterly immeasurable.
All Tathāgatas speak this in unison: the karmic fruits of the world are inconceivable;
as dragons transform clouds and water, so the Buddha enters meditative absorption, and within that absorption, his transformations are beyond thought.
Seeing that he had emerged and taught but a small portion, the entire assembly was struck with wonder;
through the skillful wisdom of the Dharma Master, they were made to understand, and as he spoke with such swift eloquence,
they were able to comprehend it and immediately attained the eight liberations.
When a śrāvaka attains one, it becomes many; or when he attains many, they are as if one. Behold that space, blazing with light;
fiercely radiant and intensely glowing, all is utterly luminous.
The city of fire reaches down through to the water wheel, where he sits and lies in peaceful dwelling;
in an instant his body transforms in an inconceivable way.
Having cast far away worldly conduct for the sake of awakening, though his body undergoes inconceivable transformations, it remains so.
Unable to benefit others, they remain within the mundane world;
yet [the Buddhas] are able to illuminate and perceive all realms in the ten directions— the ponds, lakes, pools, marshes, and deep springs,
as well as the square, round, large, and small seas and rivers of jewels— all of which manifest inconceivable forms and appearances.
Just as the sun illuminates the ten directions, And as wisdom liberates through all samādhis, So too is it when one sees the Tathāgata Buddha.
Each manifests their form therein: Sharp swords, bows, blades, arrows, and armor.
With helmets, arm-guards, and iron scale-armors, adorned as if with various colors;
beholding that Tathāgata’s net of light, they distinguish neither hatred nor love, free from doubt,
through the samādhi of the merit of liberation.
Even unto the ocean of sentient beings’ births, They hear what is taught and know it all;
their own speech is filled with joy.
They can understand all according to their various types, Having attained the power of the wondrous dhāraṇī-dharma.
Transcending existence and non-existence in the human and celestial realms, he is named Durlabharāja; a Brahmin woman praised him, for his aspiration was free from attachment and aversion.

By being free from envy, one attains a transcendent body; yet though one possesses eloquence, if attachment and aversion remain, one cannot accomplish the great practice of giving (*mahādānapāramitā*).
There is no one who does not delight in the merit of wisdom, just as a wise man creates illusions through his skillful art.
They can manifest various boundless forms, whether by day, night, month, or in a single thought-moment.
A hundred years are like a candle in the wind; how could such illusory transformations give rise to love or hatred?
Worldly changes are like illusions and dreams; one must certainly know that they are far removed from liberation.
As those who have well-cultivated wisdom are loved by all, when the devas and asuras engage in battle, the devas prevail and the asuras retreat in dispersal;
with canopies covering their superior chariots, their armor and weapons fall away as they flee.
Yet the asuras harbor feelings of attachment and hatred toward them.
He himself declares his own transformations to be inconceivable; In wealth, nobility, and valor, none can equal him.
His manifested bodies transform in such a manner that he can uphold great nāgas and vajras;
Śakra and his retinue ride upon a great elephant, Upon whose heads appear the thirty-three [gods].
Each one further manifests six tusks; upon each tusk appear seven ponds, and within the ponds appears water, all overflowing to the brim.
Within each pond appear seven lotus flowers, adorned with various kinds of splendor; within each flower, seven more appear once again.
The goddesses know them all completely; they understand song, dance, and various musical performances.
They enjoy themselves together with Śakra and the hosts of devas, yet they know their own bodies are in the form of nāgas.
They attain the power to manifest transformations identical to all others, creating various kinds of adornments and displays.

At times he manifests as a supreme nāga; though he appears to possess desire, hatred, and delusion, he displays miraculous transformations according to his own meritorious karma, acting in accordance with the power of wisdom and skillful means.
Without samādhi, one cannot perform such deeds; it is like the manifestation of Rāhu’s body:

he transforms his feet into vajra-bonds, manifests his body in the ocean with the water reaching only to his navel, and makes his head equal in height to Mount Sumeru—yet he still possesses craving, hatred, greed, anger, and delusion.

Such is the supernatural power of the deity Rāhu; though the Māra-king destroys the Lamp of the World, if he were to manifest his supernormal transformations, they would be boundless, like the inconceivable manifestations of Śakra.
When the devas and asuras were engaged in battle, he subdued the asuras so that they could not transform;
manifesting his own body before Śakra, he was able to discern the courageous power of the asuras.
At the same time, they went before Śakra, each grasping a vajra;
the asuras seized them and trembled, as he manifested a thousand eyes capable of striking fear.
The Vajradhara of blazing radiance, clad in armor and possessed of great power, causes the asuras to retreat upon seeing him;
they are unable to withstand him due to the power of their meager merit.
Śakra manifests divine transformations for the sake of the devas, capable of saving all the worlds;
he speaks of these inexhaustible merits of divine transformation as the celestial drum in the sky exhorts the devas.

He speaks of the karmic retributions for those multitudes; knowing that the devas are addicted to sensual pleasures, the celestial drum sounds forth to deliver them, observing that the body is impermanent and does not endure for long.
The self-nature of these things cannot be comprehended; they are like illusions, like clouds obscuring the stars and moon.
The self-nature of all phenomena is like awakening from a dream.
Only by attaining the nectar [of liberation] can one leave behind impermanence; if there were any pleasure to be found therein, one would surely be attached to it.
Impermanence is as swift as a makara;
the Noble One increases in all things. Those who delight in sensual pleasures are like the blind;
yet those who hear the Dharma escape impermanence.
And for the hosts of devas, it proclaims the sublime Dharma, constantly expounding wondrous speech and extensively explaining the boundless afflictions.
The celestial drum emits great sounds, manifesting various colors according to the intentions of the devas.
Extensively for all sentient beings who are without action,
the divine drum in the sky— surpassing them by the power of celestial merit— exhorts devas and humans,
emitting a multitude of sounds that are entirely identical to theirs.
One attains birth far removed from the terrors of armies; the hosts of the Asura kings retreat and disperse of their own accord, and every moment of fear is utterly eliminated.
One rescues all the worlds, becoming free from the hosts of the Māra-king of afflictions.
Not being subject to afflictions, they are said to dwell in bliss;

their emanation bodies cause all others to rejoice. Each illusory body is identical to theirs, and among all the celestial maidens, each displays herself in the same way; at that same time, all the women experience the pleasure of desire.
If one dwells within the wondrous Dharma of intrinsic nature, one reveals and expounds that wondrous Dharma.
In a single kṣaṇa, Śakra performs divine transformations; yet Śakra possesses craving, hatred, and delusion, finding delight only among his own retinue.
There is no one in the world who constantly employs skillful means.
The world’s transformations are free from desire, yet Māra dwells in the world of strife and contention;
he subdues all classes of sentient beings, and the power of afflictions and karma binds them all universally.
Deluded and ignorant beings cannot escape; they possess craving, anger, and delusion.
All worlds are encompassed by the Demon King, dwelling within the ten paths of action.

All worlds are self-destructive; from the palaces of the Brahmā Kings and the lords of the three thousandfold world-systems, even unto the Brahmā palaces of the three thousandfold world-systems, he universally manifests his body and dwells therein.
The Brahmā King utters a wondrous sound; within that world, the Brahmā King surely knows he can manifest transformations, such that those passing kalpas are like a mere instant.
Unable to give rise to a single thought of compassion and wisdom, once the three calamities have passed and the kalpa of destruction is over, the inconceivable mind pervades all worlds;
from the karmic retribution of sentient beings, the winds of the mind arise.
The wind can bring to completion the vessel-world, including the four seas, the myriad mountains, and the celestial palaces;
it can produce vast seeds, radiant jewels, and clouds from which rain falls.
The rain ceases, the wind subsides, and the clouds naturally withdraw; the wind can bring to maturity all that exists in the world and bring peace and happiness to the many realms of existence.
Though they have not studied the *pāramitās*, nor studied the qualities of a Buddha, they are able to manifest inconceivable wonders in the world.
Though such a person exists, no one can perceive them; yet even the sounds of flying birds and running beasts,
the voices of women, boys, and girls, the thundering roar of clouds and lightning, and the sound of the ocean tide—
all sentient beings hear and know each of these, yet each hears only the sound of their own nature.
By means of vast, unimpeded eloquence and knowledge, Each river produces a vast sound, as do the wondrous musical tones that delight the world.
They are able to gather all the oceans of sentient beings; Just as the ocean obtains wondrous jewels and inexhaustible waters.
Though rivers and streams pour forth in competition, they do not increase;
likewise, the merit of concentration, wisdom, liberation, and deliverance is inexhaustible. From the wisdom of wisdoms, all merits are produced, yet even the merit thus obtained does not increase.
Ascending from below to the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations, he spreads clouds of loving-kindness across the four great continents,
adorned with countless varieties.
These clouds manifest everywhere in myriad exquisite colors, some transforming into the brilliant radiance of red pearls.
In Tuṣita Heaven it has the color of gold and snow; In the Yāma Heaven it is vaidūrya;
In the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven it is a treasury of lapis lazuli; In the Cāturmahārājika Heaven it is the color of crystal;
It has the color of a sea-cloud of adamantine solidity; And in the palace of the kinnaras, its fragrance wafts afar.
The color of a lotus within the palace of the Dragon King, The dark black of firm and great strength,
The color of mountain rock in the palace of the Asuras, The color of exquisite golden light like a mirage,
Various adornments of foreign lands and other regions, And the azure-green hue of Jambudvīpa.
The colors of the clouds each change according to the continent,
like the hues of lightning and sunlight; their wondrous colors are equal to the pure moon,
while those of Tuṣita Heaven are golden-purple, and those of Yāma Heaven are like gold and snow.
In the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, it is the color of lapis lazuli; In the realm of the Four Great Kings, it is the color of crystal.
It is the color of the firm diamond and the ocean-clouds; The palace of the kinnaras is filled with fragrance;
Within the palace of the nāga kings, it is the color of a lotus. Firmly maintaining great power, it is the color of black.
The palaces of the asuras have the hue of iron mountains, yet they are illuminated by supremely exquisite and pure maṇi-jewels, adorned with various distinctions.
Wherever the lightning flashes reach, it is like clouds; so too are the heavens of Nirmāṇarati and Brahmā.
The sounds of drums manifest simultaneously, pervading everywhere:
the voices of celestial maidens in the palace of Yama; the sounds of the Gandharvas in the Heaven of the Four Great Kings;
the clashing of mountains and the tide of the ocean; the flutes of the Kinnaras and the sounds of the Kiṃnaras.
The voice of the kalaviṅka bird in the dragon palaces, The voices of the nāga maidens within their firm abodes,
The sounds of lutes and zithers in the asura palaces, Human voices, the sound of the ocean, and the resonance of flutes;
The wondrous fragrance of the gods of Nirmāṇarati, And rains of various flowers, all serving as adornments.
Within the wondrous maṇi moon and the wondrous lunar disc, there are garlands of māndārava flowers and fragrant ointments;
possessing the color of maṇi jewels from Tuṣita Heaven, they are adorned with various kinds of exquisite gems.
Like moonlight, the maṇi-jewel crest, and a profuse, swirling rain of golden robes;
with various banners, streamers, and precious parasols; adorned with ointments, fragrant flowers, and garlands;
and with golden pearls and crimson garments—these rain down constantly within the Yāma heaven.
In the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, there are wish-fulfilling jewels, Sandalwood and aloeswood for unguents,
Gośīrṣa flowers and celestial, exquisite garlands, Fragrant waters and rains of various wonderful blossoms,
And rare delicacies that increase one’s strength; Obtaining fragrant and delicious flavors, their countenances are joyful and serene.
Extraordinary, wondrous jewels, inconceivable, Rain down upon the palaces of the Four Heavenly Kings and the dragon realms;
They rain upon the great ocean with steadfast persistence, Thus immeasurable and inexhaustible.
The treasuries are inexhaustible and most vast, constantly raining down boundless, supreme, and wondrous jewels;
they are filled with the adornment of exquisite garments, and furthermore rain powdered incense and *mālatī* flowers.
Sometimes they produce the elegant and wonderful sounds of lutes and zithers, while the *kiṃnara* maidens rain down necklaces and ornaments.
The dragon palaces constantly rain red pearls;
they shatter the bows of enemies with agility. Within the palaces of the asuras, swords and halberds rain down, while priceless necklaces bring them peace.
It rains upon the pure kulaṇḍas, raining further various kinds of wondrous lamp-lights;
the people of Jambudvīpa all rejoice.
Flower trees, fruit trees, and fragrant trees—these wondrous celestial objects bring peace to the world.
Thus, the adornment of clouds is inconceivable, And the adornment of thunderclaps and rain is likewise;
Such transformations of the dragons are beyond thought.
The manifestations of these dragons are supreme and inconceivable; If one enters into the ocean of the Dharma’s merits, [they become even more so].
Boundless transformations are beyond measure;
thus has that Tamer of Men spoken. This courageous wisdom is beyond analogy;
this gateway to liberation in which he now abides is declared the supreme liberation.
The vast, subtle, and unsurpassed intention; The unprecedented and true intention;
Such a supreme and profound intention— This Dharma is difficult to practice and most rare.

Among all those who practice the path in this world, if they hear of this supreme liberation, they will be honored and praised by the world; for such a path for sentient beings is difficult to encounter.
Thus, one who can revere this Dharma and perform meritorious deeds will obtain peace and happiness;
by honoring it through the power of causes for oneself and others, one shall be free from doubt within the human world.
They do not give rise to doubt regarding the Śrāvaka vehicle, nor likewise regarding the Pratyekabuddha vehicle;
they further harbor no doubt concerning the many vehicles—thus abiding in the Mahāyāna is not difficult for them.
To revere this sutra is exceedingly rare; how then can one read, recite, and uphold it?
If one abides in this Dharma, how should one practice?
Even if one were to carry upon one's head all the mountains and oceans of the trichiliocosm for as many kalpas as there are in the future, such diligent toil would not be difficult.
To show reverence for this sutra is exceedingly difficult.
Even if sentient beings as numerous as the motes of dust in three thousandfold worlds were each to dwell before it for an entire kalpa, such supreme merit would not be considered difficult;
rather, to have faith in this sutra is truly difficult.
Even if one were able to hold within the palm of one's hand the mountains and oceans of ten buddha-fields, such arduous effort would not be difficult;
yet, to revere this sutra is exceedingly rare to attain.
To remain before each and every sentient being, as numerous as the atoms within ten buddha-fields, for the duration of an eon—even such a most supreme reward of merit is not difficult to attain;
yet, those who have faith in this sutra are exceedingly rare to find.
If one dwells before each [Buddha] for an entire eon, yet reads, recites, and upholds this Dharma,
its merit surpasses the former by an ayuta.
If one were able to subdue the palaces of the Māras in all the lands of the ten directions, [the merit of upholding this Dharma would still be greater].
Guiding [beings] without fault, all are brought to peace and security.
From his mouth, he manifests everything; extending his hand, he places it upon the crown of his head.
Possessing boundless merit and universal auspiciousness, he emerges from the mouths of all Tathāgatas.
The Tathāgata stroked his head with his hand and said, "You should skillfully expound this Dharma-gate of liberation.
You all should cause it to spread widely, lest this Dharma be severed.
After the World-Honored Buddha had spoken these verses, he remained silent and dwelt in stillness.
At that time, all the devas and the assembly of noble beings from the great trichiliocosm, including the multitude of people gathered like an ocean, spoke with one voice:
"This is the Tathāgata’s second turning of the wheel of Dharma; we praise it, saying, 'Excellent!'"
Well-spoken, World-Honored One! It is rare, it is rare indeed!
We have never before heard such a true Dharma being taught.
If there are sentient beings who hear this true Dharma, they will be most rare indeed!
They immediately cease to be born into poor or lowly families, and their minds attain equanimity, as if they had made offerings to and honored a multitude of Tathāgatas.
These sentient beings, in turn, instruct one another as if they were Buddha-stūpas and shrines.
Those sentient beings—whether in the heavens or among humans—cannot be harmed by the retinues of Māra.
Neither can they be harmed by those humans or devas who are householders or renunciants, nor by kings, ministers, elders, or officials.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the Tathāgata has obtained such a rare thing as this *Ratnaprabhāsa-sūtra*, so that its true Dharma may circulate in the world?”
These jewels among all the sutras have appeared in the world solely through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, that these sentient beings are able to hear this Dharma is likewise due to the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata.
At that time, the World-Honored One again opened his golden mouth and addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
“Ānanda, you should receive and uphold this True Dharma;
with a diligent mind and energetic effort, receive, uphold, read, and recite it.”
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda circumambulated the Buddha three times and spoke these words:
“World-Honored One!
I shall receive and uphold such True Dharma, never forgetting or losing it.”

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the entire assembly of noble bodhisattvas—such as Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, and the Venerable Śāriputra and other great śrāvakas—as well as the devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they prostrated and departed.
